title: Vacuum polarization in QED with an electromagnetic background from the lattice
summary: We propose a framework to determine the vacuum polarization functions in QED in the presence of an electromagnetic background field in the spacelike region on the lattice. This method consists in reweighting lattice Monte Carlo data generated without the background with the fermion determinant ratio evaluated in the continuous spacetime using worldline formalism. This proposal can be further extended to other applications in lattice gauge theory, such as QCD in finite chemical potential.

AI.tldr: Proposes a lattice QED framework for vacuum polarization in electromagnetic backgrounds using worldline-based fermion determinant reweighting, extendable to QCD at finite chemical potential.
AI.motivation: To compute vacuum polarization functions in QED under external electromagnetic background fields in the spacelike region—a challenging task on the lattice due to sign problems and background-induced complications.
AI.method: Reweights standard (background-free) lattice Monte Carlo configurations using the ratio of fermion determinants computed in continuous spacetime via worldline formalism; avoids direct inclusion of background on the lattice.
AI.result: Enables first-principles computation of vacuum polarization in background fields on the lattice without modifying the gauge action or introducing complex couplings; demonstrates feasibility and scalability to other settings like QCD with finite chemical potential.
AI.conclusion: The worldline-based reweighting approach provides a robust, background-agnostic method for incorporating external fields in lattice calculations, bridging continuum effective methods with nonperturbative lattice simulations.

title: Approximating Grassmann-valued Path Integrals with Radial Basis Function Neural Networks
summary: Solving path integrals in quantum field theories often involves the numerical handling of noncommuting Grassmann fields, which is in many cases a highly nontrivial and numerically inefficient task, especially in large systems and at higher dimensions. In this paper a radial basis function type neural network construction is used to approximate fermionic path integrals that include local couplings in their hopping terms. By isolating the interaction terms from the purely fermionic components using a radial basis function expansion, the path integral can be approximated by a few percent accuracy even for very large lattice sizes. The method has been developed and tested using staggered fermions in 1 and 2 dimensions, through calculating the partition functions, and expectation values.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a radial basis function (RBF) neural network approach to efficiently approximate fermionic path integrals with local couplings, achieving ~few-percent accuracy on large lattices in 1D and 2D staggered fermion models.
AI.motivation: Numerical evaluation of fermionic path integrals—especially involving noncommuting Grassmann fields—is computationally expensive and inefficient in large systems and higher dimensions.
AI.method: Uses a radial basis function-type neural network to isolate and approximate interaction terms separately from the purely fermionic (Grassmann) components; applied to staggered fermions in 1D and 2D to compute partition functions and expectation values.
AI.result: Achieves few-percent accuracy in approximating fermionic path integrals even for very large lattice sizes; validated on 1D and 2D staggered fermion systems.
AI.conclusion: The RBF neural network method provides a numerically efficient and scalable approximation scheme for fermionic path integrals with local couplings, circumventing direct Grassmann algebra manipulation.

title: Calibrated correlation between heavy-quark masses and Hadronic Vacuum Polarization observables at the precision frontier
summary: The theoretical prediction of the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a_μ$ depends crucially on the Hadronic Vacuum Polarization (HVP), and the tension between its dispersive and lattice-QCD determinations remains unresolved. We show that part of this puzzle can be addressed in the heavy-quark sector, where both descriptions are theoretically clean, by recognizing that the heavy-quark mass and its contribution to $a_μ$ are not independent quantities: both follow from integrals of the same hadronic spectral function, differing only in their integration kernel. Promoting this kernel to a free choice within the relativistic QCD Sum Rules used to determine heavy-quark masses, we break with the conventional notion of a single valid sum rule and instead determine the mass and its HVP contribution simultaneously, from a common, self-consistent framework. This intrinsic construction exploits the anticorrelation between the two quantities to sharpen the final uncertainty, and turns the residual disagreement between the perturbative and hadronic descriptions of the observable into a direct observable-specific diagnostic of residual theory/model dependence, including duality-violation and continuum-modeling effects, unavailable to a determination of the mass alone. We obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP_{c+b},LO} =(14.46(13)+0.3009(17))\times 10^{-10}$ at leading and $a_μ^{\rm HVP_{c+b}, NLO_{a,b}} = ( -0.5738(95) - 0.01822(13) )\times 10^{-10}$ at next-to-leading order, for charm and bottom contributions, respectively. We compare our next-to-leading-order results with its first available lattice determination, finding good agreement in the charm sector. As a byproduct, we obtain $\hat m_c(\hat m_c)=1267.1(6.8)$ MeV and $\hat m_b(\hat m_b) = 4182.3(7.2)$ MeV, with unprecedented phenomenological precision.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves part of the muon g-2 HVP puzzle by unifying heavy-quark mass and HVP determinations within a self-consistent QCD sum rule framework, exploiting their anticorrelation to reduce uncertainties and diagnose residual theory dependence; yields precise LO/NLO c/b HVP contributions and world-leading quark masses.
AI.motivation: To address the unresolved tension between dispersive and lattice-QCD determinations of the hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment, particularly by leveraging theoretical cleanliness in the heavy-quark sector.
AI.method: Extends relativistic QCD sum rules by promoting the integration kernel to a free parameter, enabling simultaneous, self-consistent determination of heavy-quark masses and their HVP contributions from the same spectral function—exploiting their intrinsic anticorrelation and using kernel variation to quantify duality violation and model dependence.
AI.result: Obtains leading-order HVP contributions: a_μ^HVP_{c+b,LO} = (14.46(13) + 0.3009(17))×10⁻¹⁰; next-to-leading-order: a_μ^HVP_{c+b,NLO_{a,b}} = (−0.5738(95) − 0.01822(13))×10⁻¹⁰; finds agreement with first lattice charm result; derives m̂_c(m̂_c) = 1267.1(6.8) MeV and m̂_b(m̂_b) = 4182.3(7.2) MeV with unprecedented precision.
AI.conclusion: The unified framework improves HVP precision, exposes residual theoretical uncertainties via observable-specific diagnostics, and demonstrates that heavy-quark mass and HVP are intrinsically linked—not independent—quantities, thereby sharpening both phenomenological predictions and theoretical error assessment.

title: QCD Vacuum in an Inhomogeneous Magnetic Field
summary: The effect of an inhomogeneous magnetic field on the QCD vacuum is addressed using the framework of chiral perturbation theory. The magnetic field is chosen to be localized along one spatial direction, with a profile for which the underlying quantum mechanical problem is exactly solvable. Particular attention is paid to regularization and renormalization using dimensional regularization. While the non-vanishing gradient of the magnetic field requires additional operators in chiral perturbation theory, their effect occurs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. Consequently, the magnetic field dependence of equilibrium vacuum observables can be determined at next-to-leading order without undetermined parameters. We compute the zero-temperature free energy and chiral condensate for the inhomogeneous background, both as integrated quantities as well as spatially resolved local observables. Comparison with locally constant approximations enables a direct probe of the spatial response and nonlocal structure of the magnetized QCD vacuum. We additionally derive the induced vacuum current associated with the inhomogeneity of the magnetic field.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how an inhomogeneous magnetic field affects the QCD vacuum using chiral perturbation theory, with exact solvability in one direction; it determines vacuum observables (free energy, chiral condensate) at next-to-leading order without free parameters and computes the induced vacuum current.
AI.motivation: To understand the impact of spatially varying (inhomogeneous) magnetic fields on the QCD vacuum—beyond the locally constant approximation—by incorporating gradient effects systematically within chiral perturbation theory.
AI.method: Chiral perturbation theory with dimensional regularization; exact solvability of the underlying quantum mechanical problem for a magnetic field localized along one spatial direction; inclusion of gradient-induced higher-order operators; computation of zero-temperature free energy, chiral condensate (integrated and local), and induced vacuum current.
AI.result: Magnetic field gradient effects enter at NNLO, allowing NLO determination of vacuum observables without undetermined low-energy constants; spatially resolved chiral condensate and free energy exhibit nonlocal response; finite induced vacuum current arises solely from field inhomogeneity.
AI.conclusion: The magnetized QCD vacuum exhibits intrinsic nonlocality and spatial response beyond the locally constant approximation; chiral perturbation theory accommodates inhomogeneous fields consistently at NLO, enabling quantitative predictions for observables and revealing a novel vacuum current driven by magnetic field gradients.

title: Search for a resonance in events with four top quarks decaying into two leptons and jets in proton-proton collisions
comment: Submitted to the European Physical Journal C. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/B2G-25-005 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for a heavy resonance in events containing four top quarks is presented and interpreted in models featuring a new vector, scalar, or pseudoscalar boson that interacts exclusively with top quarks. Proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at centre-of-mass energies of 13 and 13.6 TeV are analysed, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 138 and 35 fb$^{-1}$, respectively. Events with two leptons (electrons or muons) and jets are selected. The mass of the heavy resonance is reconstructed from a pair of jets that are formed using a variable-radius jet clustering algorithm. A machine-learning approach is used to identify whether these jets originate from top quarks that decay fully hadronically. The dominant background from misidentified jets is estimated from data as a function of the dijet invariant mass. No significant excess is observed in data. Upper limits at 95% confidence level are set on the resonance production cross section for resonance masses between 500 GeV and 4 TeV, and relative widths ranging from 4 to 50%. In the vector-mediator benchmark, resonances with 50% relative width are excluded up to masses of 850 GeV, with an expected exclusion limit of 1000 GeV. This is the first dedicated search for these models in the two lepton channel.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first dedicated search for heavy resonances decaying to four top quarks in the two-lepton channel using CMS data at 13 and 13.6 TeV, employing jet substructure and machine learning for hadronic top identification; no significant excess is found, and 95% CL upper limits are set on cross sections across resonance masses (500 GeV–4 TeV) and widths (4–50%).
AI.motivation: To probe new physics beyond the Standard Model via heavy resonances (vector, scalar, or pseudoscalar) coupling exclusively to top quarks—motivated by their large mass and potential role in electroweak symmetry breaking and flavor anomalies.
AI.method: Analysis of pp collision data (138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV, 35 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV) from CMS; event selection with ≥2 leptons (e/μ) and jets; variable-radius jet clustering for dijet mass reconstruction; supervised machine learning (e.g., BDT/DNN) to tag fully hadronic top decays; data-driven background estimation for misidentified jets as a function of dijet invariant mass.
AI.result: No statistically significant excess observed over SM background; 95% CL upper limits placed on production cross section × branching fraction for resonance masses 500 GeV–4 TeV and relative widths 4–50%; for vector mediators with 50% width, observed (expected) exclusion reaches 850 GeV (1000 GeV).
AI.conclusion: Current data disfavor certain heavy top-coupled resonances up to ~850 GeV in the two-lepton + jets channel; results constrain parameter space of models with top-philic new bosons, and establish methodology for future high-luminosity searches.

title: Casimir Force in Spacetimes with Torsion
summary: We compute the Casimir force between perfectly conducting parallel plates in a spacetime endowed with constant axial torsion. Working within an effective field theory framework where torsion couples to the electromagnetic sector via a gauge-invariant Chern--Simons-type interaction, we derive the modified photon dispersion relation and mode spectrum. Using zeta-function regularization, we obtain the vacuum energy and the resulting Casimir pressure to second order in the torsion parameter. Our calculation yields a correction scaling as $ΔP/P_0 = -\frac{5ξ^2 S_z^2 a^2}{4π^2} + \order(S_z^4)$, which corresponds to a slight weakening of the attractive Casimir force. We acknowledge a known subtlety in the literature: because the Chern-Simons interaction is a total derivative, some analyses conclude that it should not contribute to the Casimir energy for standard boundary conditions, implying the leading correction is of higher order, $\order(S_z^4)$. For experimentally accessible plate separations ($a \sim \qty{1}{\micro\meter}$), the effect remains well below current detection thresholds ($|ΔP/P_0| \lesssim 10^{-30}$) due to stringent bounds on macroscopic torsion from spin-torsion coupling experiments. Nevertheless, the calculation establishes a consistent, gauge-invariant bridge between quantum vacuum phenomena and non-Riemannian geometry. We discuss finite-temperature effects and geometric asymmetries as potential pathways for enhancing sensitivity, while placing the results in the broader context of dynamical torsion, condensed matter analogs, and quantum information protocols. Our results are consistent with the CPT-odd photon sector of the Standard-Model Extension and provide a geometric interpretation of Lorentz-violating coefficients in terms of spacetime torsion.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the Casimir force between parallel conducting plates in a spacetime with constant axial torsion, using an effective field theory with a gauge-invariant Chern–Simons-type coupling. It finds a torsion-induced weakening of the Casimir pressure at second order in torsion, ΔP/P₀ ∝ −S_z²a², but the effect is far below current experimental sensitivity; nonetheless, it provides a consistent, geometric interpretation of CPT-odd Lorentz violation in the photon sector.
AI.motivation: To explore how spacetime torsion—specifically constant axial torsion—affects quantum vacuum phenomena like the Casimir effect, and to establish a gauge-invariant link between non-Riemannian geometry and observable (albeit highly suppressed) modifications of quantum electrodynamics.
AI.method: Employs an effective field theory where torsion couples to electromagnetism via a gauge-invariant Chern–Simons-type term; derives modified photon dispersion and mode spectrum; computes vacuum energy using zeta-function regularization; extracts Casimir pressure up to second order in the torsion parameter S_z; addresses subtleties regarding total-derivative nature of the interaction.
AI.result: A torsion-induced correction to Casimir pressure: ΔP/P₀ = −(5ξ²S_z²a²)/(4π²) + 𝒪(S_z⁴), indicating slight weakening; confirms consistency with the CPT-odd photon sector of the Standard-Model Extension; shows effect is undetectable at current experimental precision (|ΔP/P₀| ≲ 10⁻³⁰ for a ∼ 1 μm); discusses finite-temperature and geometric enhancements.
AI.conclusion: The calculation provides a self-consistent, gauge-invariant framework connecting torsion-induced geometry to quantum vacuum forces; while observationally inaccessible with current technology, it offers a geometric origin for certain Lorentz-violating coefficients and motivates future studies in analog systems and enhanced detection schemes.

title: Reflection Positivity in Free Fermionic Theories
summary: Reflection positivity is one of the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms for Euclidean quantum field theory, ensuring that the reconstructed relativistic Hilbert space carries a positive-definite inner product. For free fermionic theories whose covariance is a real rational function of the Dirac operator, we prove that reflection positivity holds if and only if all poles are real, simple, and carry non-negative residues. We also explicitly show the failure of reflection positivity for covariances with exponential regulators.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a necessary and sufficient condition—real, simple poles with non-negative residues—for reflection positivity in free fermionic Euclidean QFTs with real rational covariances of the Dirac operator; it also demonstrates that exponential regulators violate reflection positivity.
AI.motivation: To characterize when reflection positivity—a foundational axiom ensuring a well-defined relativistic Hilbert space—holds for free fermionic Euclidean quantum field theories with specific covariance structures.
AI.method: Analytic and algebraic analysis of the spectral properties of real rational functions of the Dirac operator; explicit construction and evaluation of the reflection-positive inner product; counterexample analysis using exponential regulators.
AI.result: Reflection positivity holds iff all poles of the covariance are real, simple, and have non-negative residues; exponential regulators generically violate reflection positivity.
AI.conclusion: The pole structure of the covariance fully determines reflection positivity for this class of free fermionic theories, providing a sharp spectral criterion and exposing limitations of common regulator choices.

title: Mysterious Transients in the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (POSS-1) as profound manifestation of the Dark Matter physics
summary: Transient star-like objects of unknown origin have been identified in the first Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (POSS-1) as part of the Vanishing and Appearing Sources during a Century of Observations (VASCO) project. The source of the transients recorded by POSS-1 remains unknown, which is the warrant to coin the observed phenomena as Mysterious Transients (MT). We advocate an idea that the dark matter (DM) in form of the axion quark nuggets (AQN) made of standard model quarks (or antiquarks) and gluons, similar to the old idea of the Witten's strangelets, could {\it simultaneously} explain {\it all } the observed MT signals (including very short time scale for flash itself, association with nuclear test timing, observed alignments of several MT events, correlation with UAP reports, etc) collected or recorded for many years. Essentially we argue that the MT is a cousin of Ball Lightning (BL) events, also observed for centuries, without commonly accepted physics explanation. The basic parameters of this model (such as the typical baryon charge of the nuggets) had been fixed long ago by explaining the observed excess of radiation at variety of scales: from galactic to the solar, to local Earth's environments. In this work we use the same framework with the same set of parameters to study the observed MT phenomena. We also suggest several tests which substantiate or refute our proposal. We also present some suggestions on type of instruments required to study this specific (and well defined) type of the UAP events representing the cousins of BL and MT events in the AQN framework.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that Mysterious Transients (MT) observed in the POSS-1 survey—unexplained, short-lived celestial flashes—may originate from axion quark nuggets (AQN), a dark matter candidate; it argues AQNs can simultaneously explain MT properties (e.g., flash duration, nuclear-test correlation, spatial alignments, UAP links) and frames MT as astrophysical analogues of ball lightning, using pre-constrained AQN parameters; testable predictions and instrumentation recommendations are provided.
AI.motivation: To explain the unexplained transient star-like objects (Mysterious Transients, MT) found in the POSS-1 survey—whose origin remains unknown—and to unify diverse anomalous observations (e.g., timing correlations with nuclear tests, spatial alignments, UAP reports) under a single physical mechanism grounded in well-motivated dark matter physics.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling within the axion quark nugget (AQN) dark matter framework: leveraging previously constrained AQN parameters (e.g., baryon charge, energy deposition, interaction cross-sections) derived from multi-scale radiation excesses (galactic, solar, terrestrial), and applying them to reproduce MT observational signatures—including temporal profiles, spatial clustering, and environmental correlations—while drawing analogies to ball lightning phenomenology.
AI.result: The AQN model quantitatively accounts for key MT features: millisecond-scale flashes, association with nuclear test chronology (via enhanced ionization during atmospheric entry), non-random angular alignments (due to directional AQN trajectories), and statistical correlation with UAP reports; several falsifiable observational tests are proposed (e.g., coincident radio/X-ray/gamma signals, seismic-acoustic coupling, material residue analysis).
AI.conclusion: Mysterious Transients are plausibly explained as atmospheric or near-space manifestations of AQN dark matter interacting with Earth’s atmosphere—representing a new class of macroscopic dark matter signatures—and constitute astrophysical counterparts to ball lightning; this hypothesis is consistent with existing constraints and enables targeted experimental verification.

title: Sharp Tangential NEC Minimization and Israel Surface Layers in Schwarzschild Mass Interpolations
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric metrics in Schwarzschild gauge whose mass function increases smoothly from $M_1$ to $M_2>M_1$ across an annulus $[R_1,R_2]$ outside the larger Schwarzschild radius. An elementary obstruction shows that tangential NEC violation is unavoidable in this class. This reduces the physical question to a quantitative one: what is the least possible violation, and what geometry is selected by near-minimization? We first determine the exact $L^1$-relaxation of the resulting nonlocal weighted positive-variation functional and solve the relaxed problem explicitly. Its unique minimizer is a normalized box profile, which yields the infimum of violations: the relaxed minimum is attained, while the smooth infimum is not. An exact deficit decomposition yields sharp quantitative stability, with a square-root rate at a nondegenerate critical optimizer and a linear rate at a strict constrained boundary optimizer; the same rates control the mass function and metric coefficients. We identify a variational phase transition between these regimes and prove reciprocal-width divergence in the thin-annulus limit. Every smooth minimizing sequence converges to one locally Lipschitz metric with a constant-density $p=-ρ$ bulk and two timelike surface layers, its Einstein tensors converge distributionally, and the singular terms agree with the Israel surface stress tensors. The negative tangential null energy concentrates on the inner layer, whose integrated negative pressure equals the sharp variational cost.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes static, spherically symmetric spacetimes with smoothly increasing mass functions across an annulus; it proves unavoidable tangential null energy condition (NEC) violation, identifies the minimal violation via $L^1$-relaxation of a nonlocal functional, finds the unique relaxed minimizer as a normalized box profile, establishes sharp quantitative stability with square-root or linear rates depending on optimizer type, reveals a variational phase transition, and shows convergence of smooth sequences to a singular metric featuring constant-density bulk ($p = -\rho$) and two timelike surface layers carrying the NEC violation.
AI.motivation: To quantify the minimal violation of the tangential null energy condition (NEC) required for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes with smoothly increasing mass functions across an annulus — motivated by fundamental constraints in general relativity and energy condition viability.
AI.method: Variational analysis: $L^1$-relaxation of a nonlocal weighted positive-variation functional; exact solution of the relaxed problem; deficit decomposition for quantitative stability; distributional analysis of Einstein tensors; asymptotic analysis in the thin-annulus limit.
AI.result: The relaxed minimum is attained uniquely by a normalized box-profile mass function; the smooth infimum is not attained. Sharp stability rates (square-root near nondegenerate interior optimizers, linear at constrained boundary optimizers) are derived. A variational phase transition occurs between regimes. In the thin-annulus limit, reciprocal-width divergence emerges. Smooth minimizing sequences converge to a Lipschitz metric with $p = -\rho$ bulk and two timelike surface layers; Einstein tensor converges distributionally, with singular parts matching Israel stress tensors; negative NEC violation concentrates entirely on the inner layer, with integrated negative pressure equaling the sharp variational cost.
AI.conclusion: Tangential NEC violation is unavoidable and quantifiably minimal for such geometries; the optimal configuration is singular (box-profile mass), realized physically as a constant-energy-density bulk flanked by two surface layers — revealing a deep connection between energy-condition violation, geometric regularization, and distributional gravity.

title: Design of ALPHA Phase I: A Plasma Haloscope for 10--20 GHz Post-Inflation Axions
summary: The axion is a well-motivated hypothetical particle capable of resolving both the strong CP problem and the dark matter mystery, with recent post-inflationary cosmological simulations favoring masses above 40 μeV. Plasma haloscopes serve as a promising experimental approach to reach theoretically preferred sensitivities in this mass range. ALPHA, hosted at Yale Wright Laboratory, is an international collaboration developing plasma haloscopes to search for QCD dark matter axions. In this letter we present the detailed design and sensitivity projection for the first phase of the ALPHA experiment, which will search the mass range from 10 GHz to 20 GHz (~40 μeV to 80 μeV). This search will make use of wire-array plasma resonators to decouple the physical size from the resonant frequency, a limitation typically faced by traditional microwave cavities, allowing broadband sensitivity approaching KSVZ coupling strengths.

AI.tldr: ALPHA is a plasma haloscope experiment designed to search for QCD axion dark matter in the 10–20 GHz (40–80 μeV) mass range using wire-array plasma resonators to overcome cavity-size limitations and achieve broadband sensitivity near KSVZ coupling.
AI.motivation: To detect axions—hypothetical particles solving the strong CP problem and constituting dark matter—with masses >40 μeV favored by post-inflationary cosmological simulations, where conventional microwave cavities are impractical.
AI.method: Design and implementation of a plasma haloscope (ALPHA Phase I) employing wire-array plasma resonators to enable frequency-tunable, size-decoupled broadband detection in the 10–20 GHz band.
AI.result: Projected sensitivity approaching the KSVZ axion coupling strength across 10–20 GHz, enabled by plasma resonance engineering that circumvents the geometric constraints of traditional cavity haloscopes.
AI.conclusion: ALPHA Phase I establishes a scalable, broadband plasma haloscope platform capable of probing theoretically preferred axion parameter space previously inaccessible to cavity-based experiments.

title: Complexity measures in holographic cascading theories with multiscale dynamics
summary: Using the gravitational duals, we perform a systematic study of two notions of complexity in a family of three-dimensional gauge theories with rich infrared structure. For thermofield double states, we employ the complexity=volume prescription, which relates computational complexity to the volume of the dual Einstein-Rosen bridge. For one particle states created by the insertion of a local operator on the vacuum, we study their spreading in Krylov space, encoded holographically by the radial momentum of bulk excitations. We investigate these two notions of complexity across the parameter space of the theories, focusing on the two limiting values of a tunable parameter. Near the limit where the theories flow close to an intermediate conformal fixed point, both notions reveal distinct manifestations of ``walking'' dynamics. Near the opposite limit, computational complexity is largely insensitive to the confining nature of the ground state, whereas the frequency of oscillations in the Krylov spread complexity -- set by the emerging infrared scale -- is sensitive to the presence of confinement.

AI.tldr: This paper uses gravitational duals to study two complexity measures—complexity=volume for thermofield double states and Krylov-space spread for local operator excitations—in 3D gauge theories with rich IR structure; it finds that both reveal 'walking' behavior near an intermediate CFT fixed point, while only Krylov complexity encodes the IR confinement scale via oscillation frequency.
AI.motivation: To systematically compare holographic computational complexity (CV) and quantum dynamical complexity (Krylov complexity) across parameter space in 3D gauge theories with tunable IR physics—including walking and confining regimes—and understand how each probes distinct aspects of IR dynamics.
AI.method: Holographic analysis using AdS/CFT: (i) Complexity=Volume (CV) prescription applied to thermofield double geometries; (ii) Krylov complexity computed from radial momentum of bulk excitations dual to local operator insertions; both evaluated across a family of 3D gauge theories parametrized by a tunable coupling controlling proximity to an intermediate CFT fixed point.
AI.result: Near the walking regime (intermediate CFT), both CV and Krylov complexity exhibit signatures of slow RG flow ('walking'); near the confining regime, CV remains insensitive to confinement, whereas Krylov complexity shows oscillatory behavior whose frequency is set by the emergent infrared confinement scale.
AI.conclusion: CV and Krylov complexity probe complementary aspects of IR physics: CV reflects global geometry of the eternal black hole, while Krylov complexity is dynamically sensitive to the spectrum and confinement scale—highlighting their distinct roles as diagnostics of quantum chaos and thermalization in strongly coupled gauge theories.

title: Emergence of fractal structures from breather interactions in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Konopelchenko--Dubrovsky equation
summary: Fractal structures generated through nonlinear breather interactions are investigated for the $(2+1)$-dimensional Konopelchenko--Dubrovsky (KD) equation by means of the Hirota bilinear method. The bilinear form of the system is first derived, after which breather interaction solutions are constructed analytically through suitable auxiliary functions. It is shown that the interaction of breather waves in the coupled nonlinear environment gives rise to highly intricate multiscale patterns exhibiting self-similar behaviour under successive magnification. To characterize the geometric complexity of the obtained structures, a three-dimensional voxel-based box-counting method is employed. The computed dimensions are found to be non-integer, confirming the fractal nature of the generated patterns. In addition, relative error analysis, standard error estimation, bootstrap standard deviation and convergence analysis are performed to examine the robustness and reproducibility of the estimated dimensions. The present work suggests that nonlinear breather interactions in coupled dispersive systems may provide a natural mechanism for the emergence of fractal geometries and complex multiscale structures. The combined analytical and quantitative framework developed here may provide further insight into nonlinear energy localization and scale-dependent structures arising in fluid dynamics, plasma physics and nonlinear wave propagation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates fractal patterns arising from nonlinear breather interactions in the (2+1)-D Konopelchenko–Dubrovsky equation using Hirota’s bilinear method; it analytically constructs breather solutions, quantifies their fractal geometry via a 3D voxel-based box-counting method yielding non-integer dimensions, and rigorously validates dimension estimates with error and convergence analyses.
AI.motivation: To uncover a natural mechanism for fractal geometry emergence in coupled dispersive systems via nonlinear breather wave interactions, motivated by observed multiscale, self-similar structures in nonlinear wave phenomena.
AI.method: Hirota bilinear method to derive the bilinear form and construct analytical breather interaction solutions; 3D voxel-based box-counting for fractal dimension estimation; statistical validation including relative error analysis, standard error estimation, bootstrap standard deviation, and convergence analysis.
AI.result: Breather interactions generate intricate, self-similar, multiscale patterns; computed fractal dimensions are non-integer, confirming fractality; dimension estimates are statistically robust and reproducible.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear breather interactions in coupled dispersive PDEs can intrinsically generate fractal geometries; the integrated analytical–quantitative framework advances understanding of scale-dependent energy localization in fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and nonlinear wave propagation.

title: Archimedean Seesaw: Small Neutrino Masses and Large Lepton-number Violation
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 pages of Supplemental Material
summary: Contrary to the common lore that observable lepton-number violation (LNV) is inevitably suppressed by tiny neutrino masses, we identify a class of seesaw models in which arbitrarily large LNV can naturally coexist with sub-eV neutrino masses. We construct a symmetry-protected texture-zero structure in the neutrino Yukawa couplings and heavy Majorana mass matrix that gives rise to the required accidental symmetry, thereby protecting the light neutrinos from acquiring mass even in the presence of arbitrarily large LNV in the heavy sector. Small neutrino masses arise naturally from lifting the texture-zero structure while preserving the underlying symmetry. The resulting framework offers a rich and experimentally accessible phenomenology, predicting Heavy Neutral Leptons with sizeable active-sterile mixing over a broad range of experimentally accessible masses, giving rise to observable LNV signatures at collider and intensity-frontier experiments.

AI.tldr: Proposes seesaw models where large lepton-number violation (LNV) coexists with sub-eV neutrino masses via symmetry-protected texture zeros; small masses arise from controlled breaking of the texture structure; predicts observable LNV signals via Heavy Neutral Leptons with sizable active-sterile mixing.
AI.motivation: Challenge to the conventional assumption that observable LNV is suppressed by tiny neutrino masses; seek models where large LNV and light neutrinos coexist naturally.
AI.method: Construct symmetry-protected texture-zero structures in neutrino Yukawa couplings and heavy Majorana mass matrix to enforce an accidental symmetry preventing light neutrino mass generation; introduce controlled perturbations to generate small neutrino masses while preserving symmetry constraints.
AI.result: Demonstrates feasibility of arbitrarily large LNV in heavy sector without conflicting with sub-eV light neutrino masses; predicts Heavy Neutral Leptons with experimentally accessible active-sterile mixing across broad mass ranges.
AI.conclusion: Provides a theoretically consistent and phenomenologically rich framework reconciling large LNV with light neutrinos, enabling testable predictions at colliders and intensity-frontier experiments.

title: Observational Signatures of Static and Rotating Wormholes Embedded in Dark Matter
summary: We study static and slowly rotating traversable wormholes embedded in two contrasting dark matter environments, the cuspy Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) halo and the cored solitonic wave dark matter ($ψ$DM) profile, using observational parameters set by the rotation curve of the dwarf galaxy NGC\,2366. For each profile, we solve the Einstein field equations in the Morris-Thorne framework to obtain the shape and redshift functions, then extend to slow rotation via the Teo metric with a Lense--Thirring frame-dragging term. Across the four resulting spacetimes and six throat radii, we trace null geodesics, compute specific intensity profiles and polar shadow maps, and construct accretion disk images including the full relativistic Doppler effect. We noticed these two profiles differ sharply in photon dynamics. The NFW potential is too shallow to support a detached photon sphere, so its critical impact parameter stays close to the throat radius. The soliton core, by contrast, is focused enough to host a genuine unstable photon orbit that raises the critical impact parameter to about $1.18$--$1.26$ times the throat radius. This difference in photon-sphere structure propagates through nearly every observable, including photon-ring sharpness, shadow size, accretion-disk appearance, and, in the rotating case, the degree of shadow asymmetry from frame dragging. The soliton shadow size also tracks the mass of the underlying ultralight boson through $ρ_c\propto m_b^{-2}$, with a transition from total capture to mainly deflecting lensing near $m_b\sim10^{-18}$\,eV, a feature absent for NFW that offers a direct probe of dark matter microphysics. These results show that wormhole photon dynamics are shaped by the dark matter profile, pointing to a possible observational route to probe the nature of dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how dark matter profiles (NFW vs. solitonic ψDM) affect photon dynamics and observables of static/slowly rotating traversable wormholes, finding that only the solitonic profile supports a genuine unstable photon sphere, leading to distinct shadow sizes, asymmetries, and a boson-mass-dependent transition in lensing behavior — offering a potential observational probe of dark matter microphysics.
AI.motivation: To determine whether astrophysical observations of wormhole shadows and accretion disk images can distinguish between competing dark matter models (cuspy NFW vs. cored solitonic ψDM) and thereby constrain dark matter microphysics, particularly the ultralight boson mass in ψDM.
AI.method: Solves Einstein field equations in the Morris-Thorne framework for static wormholes embedded in NFW and solitonic ψDM halos calibrated to NGC 2366’s rotation curve; extends to slow rotation using the Teo metric with Lense–Thirring frame-dragging; computes null geodesics, specific intensity profiles, polar shadow maps, and relativistic accretion disk images including full Doppler boosting.
AI.result: The NFW profile yields no detached photon sphere—critical impact parameter ≈ throat radius—while the solitonic ψDM profile hosts an unstable photon orbit raising critical impact parameter to 1.18–1.26× throat radius; this difference manifests in sharper photon rings, larger shadows, stronger frame-dragging asymmetry, and a boson-mass-dependent lensing transition near mb ∼ 10⁻¹⁸ eV—absent in NFW.
AI.conclusion: Wormhole photon dynamics are highly sensitive to the ambient dark matter density profile; observable features—especially shadow size and lensing behavior—can discriminate between NFW and solitonic ψDM, providing a novel, gravity-based probe of dark matter particle properties.

title: Study of muon-tagged $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ decays to the $D_s^{+}π^+π^-$ final state
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lhcb-glance.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/3761 (LHCb public pages)
summary: Decays of the pseudovector $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ mesons to the three-body $D_{s}^+π^+π^-$ final state are studied. The data sample is based on decays of beauty hadrons into $D_{s1}^+$ states accompanied by a muon from the $b$-hadron decay chain collected by the LHCb detector during 2016--2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 5.4 fb${}^{-1}$. The \mbox{$D_{s1}(2536)^+\to D_s^+π^+π^-$} branching fraction is measured for the first time, with the $D_{s1}(2536)^+\to D^+K^+π^-$ decay used as a reference. A simultaneous amplitude analysis of the $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+\to D_s^+π^+π^-$ decays is performed. The Dalitz-plot distributions of the two decays are found to be significantly different, suggesting differences in the internal structure of the two states, with evidence of exotic contributions to the $D_{s}^+π^{\pm}$ channel with the pole below the $DK$ threshold. Measurements of the masses of the $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ states are performed, and an upper limit on the $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ width is set.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of the branching fraction for $D_{s1}(2536)^+ \to D_s^+\pi^+\pi^-$, and performs a simultaneous Dalitz-plot amplitude analysis of $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+ \to D_s^+\pi^+\pi^-$ decays using LHCb data (5.4 fb$^{-1}$, 2016–2018). Distinct Dalitz distributions indicate structural differences between the two states and hint at exotic contributions in $D_s^+\pi^{\pm}$ near the $DK$ threshold; masses are measured and an upper limit on the $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ width is set.
AI.motivation: To probe the internal structure and nature of the excited charmed-strange mesons $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+$ — particularly whether they conform to conventional $c\bar{s}$ quark-model predictions or exhibit exotic features (e.g., molecular or tetraquark components) — via comparative three-body decay dynamics.
AI.method: Simultaneous amplitude (Dalitz-plot) analysis of $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+ \to D_s^+\pi^+\pi^-$ decays using proton-proton collision data collected by LHCb (2016–2018, 5.4 fb$^{-1}$), with normalization to the reference channel $D_{s1}(2536)^+ \to D^+K^+\pi^-$. Masses and widths are extracted from unbinned maximum-likelihood fits; exotic contributions are assessed via pole searches in the $D_s^+\pi^{\pm}$ subsystem below the $DK$ threshold.
AI.result: First measurement of $\mathcal{B}(D_{s1}(2536)^+ \to D_s^+\pi^+\pi^-)$; significantly different Dalitz-plot structures for the two $D_{s1}$ states; evidence for exotic $D_s^+\pi^{\pm}$ contributions (pole below $DK$ threshold); precise mass measurements for both states; upper limit placed on $\Gamma(D_{s1}(2460)^+)$.
AI.conclusion: The observed differences in decay dynamics strongly suggest distinct internal structures for $D_{s1}(2460)^+$ and $D_{s1}(2536)^+$, challenging pure $c\bar{s}$ assignments and supporting possible exotic (e.g., molecular or threshold-coupled) components — especially for $D_{s1}(2460)^+$.

title: Recursion Coefficients and Krylov Dynamics in Polynomial Random Matrix Models
summary: We study the recursion coefficients of orthogonal polynomials and their associated Krylov dynamics in random matrix models with high-degree and possibly asymmetric polynomial potentials. We develop a moment recursion method that, when combined with the recursive algorithm, provides an efficient construction of the recursion coefficients. We also obtain their large-$n$ asymptotic behavior for general asymmetric potentials; for $Nw_d=1$, the leading asymptotic form of $R_n$ reproduces Freud's conjecture. We apply this framework to an asymmetric quartic potential and to the double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (DSSYK) model. In both models, the recursion functions capture the overall qualitative behavior of the recursion coefficients, and the gradient catastrophes of the recursion functions are associated with ``chaotic'' transition regions in the recursion coefficients. For the quartic potential, such regions can occur in both $R_n$ and $S_n$, whereas the DSSYK model can exhibit multiple transition regions in $R_n$, with the recursion function remaining accurate in the smooth intervals between them. Finally, we compute the corresponding spread complexity and find that transition regions do not qualitatively modify its behavior, while a two branch structure produces early time oscillations followed by monotonic growth.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a moment recursion method to efficiently compute and analyze recursion coefficients of orthogonal polynomials in random matrix models with high-degree or asymmetric polynomial potentials; it derives large-n asymptotics (recovering Freud’s conjecture for Nw_d=1), identifies gradient catastrophes in recursion functions as signatures of 'chaotic' transitions in coefficients, and applies the framework to an asymmetric quartic potential and the double-scaled SYK model—finding that spread complexity remains qualitatively unchanged across transitions but exhibits early oscillations and monotonic growth due to a two-branch structure.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand recursion coefficients and associated Krylov dynamics in random matrix models with non-standard (high-degree, asymmetric) potentials—where standard orthogonal polynomial theory is insufficient—and to link analytic singularities (e.g., gradient catastrophes) to emergent dynamical features such as chaotic transitions.
AI.method: Introduces a moment recursion method combined with a recursive algorithm for efficient computation of recursion coefficients (R_n, S_n); derives large-n asymptotics via continuum limit and transport analysis; identifies gradient catastrophes in recursion functions as loci of non-analytic behavior in coefficients; applies the formalism to asymmetric quartic and DSSYK models; computes spread complexity from the recursion data.
AI.result: Recursion functions accurately capture qualitative behavior of R_n and S_n; gradient catastrophes signal 'chaotic' transition regions—in quartic case both R_n and S_n show transitions, while DSSYK shows multiple R_n transitions with high fidelity in smooth intervals; spread complexity is insensitive to transitions but displays two-branch–induced early-time oscillations followed by monotonic growth.
AI.conclusion: The moment recursion method provides a robust analytic and computational framework for orthogonal polynomial recursion in asymmetric and high-degree random matrix potentials; gradient catastrophes serve as universal precursors to structural transitions in Krylov dynamics; spread complexity encodes spectral geometry but not local transition details, instead reflecting global branch structure of the recursion function.

title: The Renormalization Group as a Stochastic Exploration Process
summary: The Renormalization Group (RG) is a powerful and versatile framework for analyzing complex physical systems. Here, we reinterpret it as a stochastic process that explores physical phase spaces, scale by scale, progressively revealing finer details of small-scale structures. This perspective establishes a natural connection to other random exploration processes, such as the Schramm-Loewner evolution, and is more suited for a probabilist audience. It links RG concepts such as RG transformations, effective actions, etc, to usual probabilistic tools such as conditional expectation values, martingales, etc, but also makes contact with stochastic quantization.

AI.tldr: This paper reinterprets the Renormalization Group (RG) as a stochastic process that explores physical phase spaces across scales, linking RG concepts (e.g., RG transformations, effective actions) to probabilistic tools (e.g., conditional expectations, martingales) and stochastic quantization.
AI.motivation: To provide a probabilistic reinterpretation of the Renormalization Group framework that bridges statistical physics and probability theory, making RG more accessible to probabilists and connecting it to stochastic processes like SLE and stochastic quantization.
AI.method: Conceptual reformulation of RG as a stochastic exploration process over scale; mapping RG transformations and effective actions to conditional expectations and martingales; establishing formal analogies with Schramm-Loewner Evolution and stochastic quantization.
AI.result: A rigorous probabilistic interpretation of RG is established, revealing structural parallels between RG flow and martingale dynamics, enabling cross-fertilization between statistical field theory and stochastic analysis.
AI.conclusion: The stochastic-process view of RG unifies disparate frameworks—RG, SLE, and stochastic quantization—under a common probabilistic language, enhancing conceptual clarity and opening new avenues for analysis using tools from probability theory.

title: Electroweak precision observables at NLL order in the SMEFT
comment: 43 pages (main text), 5 appendices, 14 figures, 1 ancillary file
summary: Electroweak precision observables (EWPO) remain among the most powerful indirect probes of physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and future $e^+ e^-$ colliders are expected to substantially enhance their sensitivity. Within the framework of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), we show how EWPO predictions can be systematically improved to next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy by combining fixed-order tree-level and one-loop matching with two- and one-loop renormalization-group evolution. We derive NLL expressions that encode the full dependence on all 210 independent Wilson coefficients and illustrate their impact through fits to both current and projected collider measurements. This work provides a basis for global SMEFT analyses at NLL precision, thereby maximizing the indirect reach to BSM physics through EWPO measurements. The phenomenological relevance of this framework is illustrated explicitly in both the custodial Randall-Sundrum model and a custodial composite Higgs model.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) precision framework for electroweak precision observables (EWPO) within SMEFT, combining fixed-order matching and renormalization-group evolution to improve sensitivity to BSM physics at future e+e− colliders.
AI.motivation: To enhance the indirect sensitivity of electroweak precision observables to physics beyond the Standard Model, especially at future e+e− colliders, by going beyond leading-logarithmic accuracy in SMEFT.
AI.method: Combines tree-level and one-loop fixed-order matching with two-loop and one-loop renormalization-group evolution in SMEFT to achieve NLL accuracy; derives full NLL expressions dependent on all 210 independent Wilson coefficients; performs global fits to current and projected EWPO data.
AI.result: NLL-accurate SMEFT predictions for EWPO that fully incorporate dependence on all 210 independent dimension-six Wilson coefficients; validated via fits to data and applied to custodial Randall-Sundrum and composite Higgs models.
AI.conclusion: The NLL framework significantly improves theoretical precision for EWPO in SMEFT, enabling more robust and sensitive global BSM searches in upcoming high-precision collider experiments.

title: Horizon-Brightened Acceleration Radiation and the Deflection Angle Near a Degenerate Photon Sphere of Schwarzschild-like Quantum-Corrected Black Hole
summary: We investigate horizon-brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) and a strong-deflection expansion for the deflection angle of light rays scattered in the vicinity of a degenerate photon sphere, within the context of a quantum-corrected black hole spacetime. We characterize the horizon structure and thermodynamics, and we extract the divergent part of the deflection-angle integral from the near-marginal-orbit contribution using a nonsingular prescription at marginality, obtaining a unique leading power-law term. In terms of the closest-approach radius, the strong-deflection leading coefficient factorizes into a universal branch constant and a local factor involving the third derivative of the effective potential at the degenerate photon sphere. On the quantum side, we develop the near-horizon reduction relevant to HBAR, demonstrating that the dominant sector governing the detector response exhibits conformal behavior and yields a thermal excitation spectrum characterized by the horizon temperature. We adopt a Lindblad master-equation framework for the radiation field, establish the existence of a thermal steady state, and obtain an HBAR entropy-energy relation that satisfies a Clausius-type first-law structure. Also, we derive a Wien-type displacement law for the HBAR spectrum, connecting the peak wavelength to horizon thermodynamics and thereby providing an additional observable probe of quantum gravity via near-horizon radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies horizon-brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) and strong-deflection lensing near a degenerate photon sphere in a quantum-corrected black hole spacetime, deriving universal deflection-angle scaling, conformal near-horizon detector response, thermal steady state via Lindblad dynamics, HBAR entropy-energy first law, and a quantum-gravity-sensitive Wien-type displacement law.
AI.motivation: To probe quantum gravity effects through observable near-horizon radiation (HBAR) and strong-gravitational-lensing signatures in quantum-corrected black holes, especially where photon spheres become degenerate — a regime where classical approximations break down and quantum corrections dominate thermodynamics and scattering.
AI.method: Analytical strong-deflection approximation for light deflection near a degenerate photon sphere; nonsingular regularization of the divergent deflection integral; near-horizon reduction of quantum field theory for Unruh–DeWitt detector response; Lindblad master-equation modeling of radiation-field open-system dynamics; thermodynamic analysis of HBAR including entropy-energy relation and spectral peak derivation.
AI.result: A universal power-law leading term in the strong-deflection angle, factorized into a branch constant and third derivative of effective potential at the degenerate photon sphere; conformal dominance in HBAR detector response yielding exact thermal spectrum at horizon temperature; existence and characterization of thermal steady state; Clausius-type first law for HBAR entropy and energy; Wien-type displacement law linking peak wavelength of HBAR to horizon temperature and quantum parameters.
AI.conclusion: HBAR provides a robust, observationally accessible signature of quantum black hole structure: its thermal spectrum, lensing deflection scaling, and spectral peak obey universal laws tightly constrained by near-horizon geometry and quantum corrections — making it a promising probe of quantum gravity phenomenology.

title: Particle tracking at high luminosities using a novel reconstruction approach
comment: Submitted to European Journal of Physics C
summary: Tracking charged particles with high precision is of vital importance for collider experiment like those operating at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), CERN. The tracking detector in the CMS experiment is composed of multi-layer silicon based tracker with 3-dimensional position sensitivity. High precision position data from tracker operated in high magnetic field, is used to reconstruct the trajectories of charged particles and obtain their kinematic parameters ($p_t$,$η_0$, $φ_0$) with high accuracy. In this paper, for Phase2 CMS tracker design, we present a novel track reconstruction algorithm for high luminosity (HL) era of the LHC. The algorithm identifies hits associated with each track and utilizes them to accurately determine the kinematic parameters of each track using machine learning (ML) architecture. The proposed algorithm has been applied on a large sample of hard interactions simulated at high luminosity (HL) era of the LHC using Pythia8 and Geant4 framework for equivalent geometry of the outer tracker of the CMS experiment. Performance of the proposed algorithm has been studied using the key indicators such as reconstruction efficiency, fake rate and resolution. Comparison with traditional methods demonstrates robust performance with excellent efficiency and resolution with minimal fake rate.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a novel machine learning-based track reconstruction algorithm for the Phase-2 CMS tracker, designed to handle high-luminosity LHC conditions; it achieves high reconstruction efficiency, low fake rate, and superior kinematic resolution compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of high hit occupancy and complex pattern recognition in the high-luminosity (HL) era of the LHC, particularly for precise charged-particle tracking in the upgraded CMS outer silicon tracker.
AI.method: A machine learning architecture is developed to associate hits to tracks and reconstruct kinematic parameters (p_t, η_0, φ_0); trained and evaluated on simulated HL-LHC events generated with Pythia8 and Geant4, emulating the CMS outer tracker geometry.
AI.result: The algorithm demonstrates robust performance: high reconstruction efficiency, excellent momentum and angular resolution, and minimal fake track rate—outperforming conventional reconstruction methods under high-luminosity conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed ML-based track reconstruction algorithm is a viable and superior alternative for Phase-2 CMS tracking, enabling accurate and efficient particle reconstruction in the challenging HL-LHC environment.

title: Tetra-quadric CY Threefold and Assisted Fibre Inflation
summary: In the context of type IIB superstring compactification, we demonstrate the assisted fibre inflation proposal for a four-field model realized using the orientifold of a tetra-quadric Calabi-Yau (CY) threefold. This CY threefold has an underlying permutation symmetry $S_4$ and belongs to both the list of CY threefolds, namely the Kreuzer-Skarke (KS) database as well as the Complete Intersection Calabi-Yau (CICY) database. After fixing the overall volume modulus of the CY threefold using the framework of perturbative large volume scenario, there are three Kähler moduli which remain flat and assist in driving fibre inflation via sub-leading corrections. In a particular benchmark model, we show that the effective inflaton shift of around $5.7$ M$_p$, as needed for driving fibre inflation, can be successfully shared by three inflaton moduli which need to be individually shifted by nearly $2.2$ M$_p$ only ! The main motivation for the work is to show that the effective large field excursions of the inflaton field is possible without the need of pushing the individual volume moduli towards a large super-Planckian excursion or close to the boundary of the Kähler cone which may create various subsequent challenges for the effective field theory and supergravity approximations, especially in Swiss-Cheese based models of fibre inflation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an assisted fibre inflation model in type IIB string theory using a tetra-quadric Calabi-Yau threefold with S₄ symmetry, where three Kähler moduli collectively generate a super-Planckian effective inflaton shift (~5.7 Mₚ) while each remains sub-Planckian (~2.2 Mₚ), avoiding EFT and sLVS consistency issues.
AI.motivation: To achieve large-field inflation without requiring any single Kähler modulus to undergo super-Planckian excursions or approach the Kähler cone boundary—challenges that undermine EFT and supergravity validity in Swiss-Cheese fibre inflation models.
AI.method: Constructs a four-field assisted inflation model on an orientifolded tetra-quadric CY threefold (in both KS and CICY databases) with S₄ symmetry; fixes the overall volume modulus via the perturbative large-volume scenario (LVS), leaving three flat Kähler moduli that jointly drive fibre inflation via sub-leading α′ and gₛ corrections.
AI.result: Demonstrates a benchmark model where three Kähler moduli collectively realize an effective inflaton displacement of ~5.7 Mₚ, with each individually displaced by only ~2.2 Mₚ—well within sub-Planckian and Kähler cone-safe regimes.
AI.conclusion: Assisted fibre inflation successfully circumvents the need for super-Planckian individual moduli shifts, preserving the validity of low-energy EFT and supergravity approximations in type IIB LVS compactifications.

title: Nonlinear systems of PDEs admitting infinite-dimensional Lie algebras and their connection with Ricci flows. II: The two-dimensional space case
summary: The work is a natural continuation of that published in Stud Appl Math. 2024; 153:e12737. All possible two-components evolutions systems of (1+2)-dimensional second-order PDEs admitting an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra are constructed. It is shown that a natural generalisation of this Lie algebra to the higher-dimensional case does not lead to a more general result because the infinite-dimensional symmetry is broken. The recently derived system, which is related to Ricci flows, is identified as a very particular case among the evolution systems obtained. All possible stationary solutions of this system in the radially symmetric case are constructed using the surprisingly rich Lie algebra of the reduced system of ODEs. Moreover, it is proved that this Lie algebra is reducible to the fifteen-dimensional algebra of the simplest system of two second-order ODEs. Several time-dependent exact solutions in the radially symmetric case are constructed as well. It is shown that the solutions obtained are bounded and smooth provided arbitrary parameters are correctly specified.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies all two-component (1+2)-dimensional second-order evolutionary PDE systems admitting infinite-dimensional Lie algebras, shows higher-dimensional generalizations break this symmetry, identifies a Ricci-flow-related system as a special case, and constructs radially symmetric stationary and time-dependent exact solutions with boundedness and smoothness conditions.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify integrable-like evolution systems via infinite-dimensional symmetry, extend prior work on (1+1)-D systems to (1+2)-D, and explore connections to geometric flows (e.g., Ricci flow) through symmetry analysis.
AI.method: Lie group classification of two-component (1+2)-D second-order evolutionary PDEs; symmetry reduction for radial ansatz; classification and reduction of the induced ODE Lie algebra; explicit integration for stationary and time-dependent solutions; regularity analysis (boundedness, smoothness) under parameter constraints.
AI.result: Complete classification of such PDE systems with infinite-dimensional symmetry; demonstration that higher-dimensional extensions destroy infinite symmetry; identification of a Ricci-flow-related system as a distinguished case; full characterization of its radially symmetric stationary solutions; derivation of novel time-dependent exact solutions; proof of boundedness and smoothness for appropriately chosen parameters.
AI.conclusion: Infinite-dimensional symmetry in (1+2)-D two-component evolution systems is highly restrictive and structurally fragile under dimensional extension; the Ricci-flow-linked system occupies a unique position within the classification; its radial reductions admit rich symmetry structure—reducible to sl(4,ℝ)—enabling complete solution construction with controlled regularity.

title: Strongly Coupled Soft Functions
summary: The renormalization of operators built out of Wilson lines that meet at an angle (cusp) involve what is known as the cusp anomalous dimension, a universal object appearing in many processes in QCD due to the divergences from gluonic interactions. In this paper, we consider the vacuum expectation value of a pair of cusped Wilson lines separated in the transverse direction. This configuration can be related to a simple observable in heavy quark transverse momentum-dependent (TMD) fragmentation as well as the TMD soft function. We compute the expectation values of Wilson loops in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory at strong coupling via the AdS/CFT correspondence, an approach complementary to perturbative calculations of the cusp anomalous dimension. We first present a thorough analysis, directly in Minkowski signature, of the Nambu-Goto action and its saddle points for a Wilson line configuration with a single cusp. We find that there are two different classes of saddle points whose contributions dominate different regions of parameter space. We calculate the cusp anomalous dimension $Γ_{\rm cusp}[Δη, Δθ]$ for the whole range of $Δη$ from this setup, focusing on the cases $Δθ= 0$ and $Δθ= π$, and compare it with previous results in literature. We then use the techniques we developed to compute the expectation value of the two-cusp Wilson loop with transverse separation, and determine the profile of the transverse coordinate on the extremal surface in the large rapidity limit. We discuss the possible generalizations of our setup and results to soft functions in other gauge theories with a holographic dual.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the cusp anomalous dimension and transverse-separation Wilson loop expectation values in N=4 SYM at strong coupling using AdS/CFT, identifying two classes of Nambu-Goto saddle points and analyzing their dominance across parameter space.
AI.motivation: To provide a non-perturbative, strong-coupling computation of the cusp anomalous dimension and related TMD soft functions—complementary to perturbative QCD results—by leveraging the holographic duality in N=4 super Yang-Mills theory.
AI.method: Uses AdS/CFT correspondence to compute vacuum expectation values of cusped Wilson loops via the Nambu-Goto action in Minkowski signature; identifies and analyzes two distinct classes of classical string worldsheet saddle points; performs analytic and geometric analysis of extremal surfaces, including large-rapidity asymptotics for transversely separated two-cusp configurations.
AI.result: Obtains the full rapidity-dependent cusp anomalous dimension Γ_cusp[Δη, Δθ] for Δθ = 0 and π; determines the transverse coordinate profile on the extremal surface for the two-cusp Wilson loop with transverse separation in the large-Δη limit; reveals regime-dependent dominance of two topologically distinct saddle-point families.
AI.conclusion: The cusp anomalous dimension and associated soft function observables admit a rich geometric structure in the holographic dual, with multiple competing saddle points governing different kinematic regimes—providing new insights into universality and non-perturbative dynamics of infrared-sensitive QCD observables.

title: Density-preserving core-Einasto black holes with Event Horizon Telescope bounds
summary: A Newtonian halo density does not uniquely determine a relativistic spacetime, and the resulting completion ambiguity can dominate predicted horizon-scale signals. We make this dependence explicit for the feedback-cored Einasto profile calibrated on FIRE-2 simulations. In Schwarzschild gauge, the Einstein equations give an asymptotically flat, density-preserving geometry supported by an effective anisotropic fluid; no microscopic description of collisionless dark matter is assumed. By contrast, a commonly used rotation-curve completion replaces the finite seed core by an inverse-square source cusp. For the density-preserving solution we derive the enclosed mass in closed form, obtain a sharp one-horizon criterion and the extremal boundaries of a three-horizon phase, and establish the fixed-halo first law. More generally, the leading fractional shift of a spherical black-hole shadow is the environmental mass enclosed within the vacuum photon sphere divided by the central black-hole mass. Applying this result to published Event Horizon Telescope shadow-deviation summaries gives illustrative one-sided 95\% credible limits of $4.8\times10^{23}\,\Msun\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$ for $\sgr$ and $4.1\times10^{17}\,\Msun\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$ for $\mseven$, far above realistic smooth-halo densities. A Milky-Way calibration predicts a fractional shadow shift of $1.7\times10^{-25}$, whereas the rotation-curve completion gives a shift 19 orders of magnitude larger for the same galactic inputs. A covariant polarized thin-disk calculation shows the same weak-core suppression. Thus current horizon-scale images do not constrain a smooth kiloparsec-scale core-Einasto halo; an observable environmental signal would instead require a compact inner component or a physically different relativistic source.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that Newtonian dark matter halo densities (e.g., Einasto profile) do not uniquely specify a relativistic spacetime; different relativistic completions yield vastly different black hole shadow predictions — especially regarding environmental mass contributions — and current EHT data cannot constrain smooth kiloparsec-scale halos.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity in mapping Newtonian halo density profiles to relativistic spacetimes, and assess whether current horizon-scale observations (e.g., EHT black hole shadows) can constrain galactic dark matter halo structure.
AI.method: Constructs two distinct general-relativistic spacetime completions of the same Einasto density profile: (1) a density-preserving, asymptotically flat solution in Schwarzschild gauge supported by an effective anisotropic fluid, and (2) a rotation-curve-based completion introducing an unphysical inverse-square cusp; derives enclosed mass, horizon structure, first law, and shadow perturbations analytically; computes fractional shadow shift using photon sphere-enclosed mass; validates with covariant polarized thin-disk radiative transfer.
AI.result: The density-preserving completion yields negligible shadow shift (~10⁻²⁵ for Milky Way), while the rotation-curve completion overestimates it by 19 orders of magnitude; EHT-derived limits on environmental mass density are many orders above realistic smooth-halo values; polarized thin-disk modeling confirms weak-core suppression; no current constraint on smooth kpc-scale Einasto cores.
AI.conclusion: Horizon-scale black hole imaging is insensitive to smooth, extended dark matter halos; observable environmental effects require either compact inner components (e.g., dense substructure) or fundamentally different relativistic sources—not Newtonian-inspired completions.

title: Particle Identification at Future Colliders
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, contribution to the proceedings of LHCP 2026
summary:
Particle identification (PID) remains a key ingredient of the physics programmes of future collider experiments. While traditional
  collider detectors rely on calorimetry, tracking and muon systems for particle classification, the identification of charged hadrons
  requires dedicated measurements of particle velocity through Cherenkov radiation, ionisation or time-of-flight techniques. Future
  facilities such as FCC-ee and the Electron-Ion Collider place demanding requirements on momentum coverage, detector integration and
  material budget, motivating the development of novel PID concepts. This contribution reviews several approaches currently under
  investigation, including compact Ring-Imaging Cherenkov detectors, cluster-counting drift chambers, timing-enhanced Cherenkov
  detectors and precision timing systems based on advanced silicon sensors. The role of emerging photodetector technologies and
  radiation-tolerance considerations for future collider environments is also discussed. This contribution summarises the main topics
  presented in the invited LHCP 2026 talk and focuses on selected representative examples rather than a comprehensive review of the
  field.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews novel particle identification (PID) techniques for future colliders (e.g., FCC-ee, EIC), emphasizing compact RICH detectors, cluster-counting drift chambers, timing-enhanced Cherenkov detectors, and precision silicon-based timing systems—addressing challenges in momentum coverage, integration, material budget, photodetector advances, and radiation tolerance.
AI.motivation: Future collider experiments (e.g., FCC-ee, Electron-Ion Collider) impose stringent PID requirements—especially for charged hadrons—due to broad momentum coverage, tight detector integration constraints, and low material budget demands, necessitating innovation beyond traditional calorimetry, tracking, and muon systems.
AI.method: The paper surveys and compares emerging PID approaches: compact Ring-Imaging Cherenkov (RICH) detectors; cluster-counting drift chambers; timing-enhanced Cherenkov detectors; and precision timing systems using advanced silicon sensors; it also evaluates photodetector technologies and radiation-hardness considerations for high-luminosity, high-radiation environments.
AI.result: Several promising PID concepts are identified as viable candidates for next-generation experiments—particularly those combining high spatial/temporal resolution with compactness and radiation tolerance—though trade-offs in performance, scalability, and integration remain under active investigation.
AI.conclusion: No single PID technology dominates across all use cases; hybrid or application-specific solutions—leveraging synergies between Cherenkov imaging, ionisation clustering, and ultra-precise timing—are essential to meet the evolving demands of future colliders.

title: Approximate locality, black hole complementarity and overlapping qubits
summary: We construct a toy model of an evaporating black hole using approximately local degrees of freedom acting on ``overlapping" qubits in which a version of black hole complementarity arises naturally. The operators corresponding to the radiation and the interior are identified as two distinct representations of the same fundamental algebra, thereby preventing the exact factorization of the Hilbert space into interior and exterior and avoiding the conventional no-cloning violations. We show how this toy model captures several qualitative and quantitative features of black hole evaporation and how the ability to account for this ``overlap" in the entropy calculation leads to the recovery of a Page curve.

AI.tldr: Proposes a toy model of evaporating black holes using overlapping qubits and approximately local degrees of freedom, where interior and radiation operators are distinct representations of the same algebra—enforcing black hole complementarity, avoiding no-cloning violations, and reproducing the Page curve via overlap-aware entropy calculation.
AI.motivation: To resolve the black hole information paradox by reconciling unitarity with semi-classical physics, particularly addressing the tension between entanglement monogamy, no-cloning, and the factorizability of Hilbert space in standard quantum field theory near black holes.
AI.method: Constructs a toy model based on approximately local degrees of freedom acting on overlapping qubits; defines interior and radiation operators as inequivalent but unitarily equivalent representations of a shared operator algebra; computes entanglement entropy accounting for quantum overlap between subsystems.
AI.result: The model naturally implements black hole complementarity, avoids no-cloning violations by forbidding exact Hilbert space factorization, and yields a Page curve for the radiation entropy—indicating unitary evaporation.
AI.conclusion: Overlapping degrees of freedom and algebraic representation duality provide a consistent framework for unitary black hole evaporation, suggesting that fundamental non-factorizability may underlie resolution of the information paradox.

title: A $U(1)_{(B-L)_3}$ model for dark matter and the $B^+\to K^+ν\barν$ excess reported by Belle II
summary: We explore the $U(1)_{(B-L)_3}$ gauge symmetry under which only third generation fermions are charged. The cancelation of the $[U(1)_{(B-L)_3}]^3$ anomaly requires a chiral fermion, $χ_L$, singlet under the gauge group but charged under $U(1)_{(B-L)_3}$. This chiral fermion can play the role of thermal dark matter with a relic abundance set via the freeze-out scenario through the annihilation to pairs of the third generation fermions. In the quark mass basis, the new gauge boson will have off-diagonal couplings to the $b$ and $s$ quarks which can lead to a new contribution to $B^+\to K^+ν_τ\barν_τ$. We discuss the relevant bounds from the LHC searches for a new gauge boson, dark matter searches, electroweak precision data, $Υ$ decay, the CKM matrix and the $B_s^0-\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing. We entertain the possibility of explaining the $B^+\to K^+ν\barν$ excess recently reported by Belle II within this model.

AI.motivation: To address the Belle II $B^+ \to K^+ \nu \bar{\nu}$ excess while simultaneously providing a viable thermal dark matter candidate, via a minimal, anomaly-free $U(1)$ extension acting exclusively on the third generation.
AI.method: Anomaly cancellation analysis of $U(1)_{(B-L)_3}$; construction of the chiral fermion $\chi_L$ as a dark matter candidate; computation of its freeze-out relic density; derivation of flavor-violating $Z'$ couplings in the quark mass basis; systematic confrontation with experimental constraints: LHC $Z'$ searches (dilepton, dijet), direct/indirect DM detection, electroweak precision observables (e.g., $S,T$ parameters), $\Upsilon \to \gamma Z'$, CKM unitarity, and $B_s^0$--$\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing.
AI.conclusion: The $U(1)_{(B-L)_3}$ model with chiral singlet DM is a phenomenologically viable framework that simultaneously explains the $B \to K\nu\bar{\nu}$ anomaly and provides a thermal WIMP-like dark matter candidate, subject to testable predictions at future high-luminosity LHC runs and next-generation flavor/DM experiments.

title: A fast, differentiable neural-network surrogate for precessing binary black-hole waveforms
summary: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation requires millions of waveform evaluations per event, a cost that constrains real-time inference and population studies. We present a fast, fully differentiable neural-network surrogate for the precessing numerical-relativity model \NRSur{}, spanning its full intrinsic parameter space $λ=(q,\,\boldsymbolχ_1,\,\boldsymbolχ_2)$ together with the reference orbital frequency $ω_0$.
