Rather than a single polarization at a fixed orientation, the surrogate predicts the \emph{inertial-frame spherical-harmonic modes} $h_{\ell m}$ ($\ell\leq 4$), so that both polarizations $h_+,h_\times$ at an arbitrary orientation $(ι,\varphi,ψ)$ are reconstructed from one network evaluation through an analytic, differentiable mode-to-strain projection. Trained on $6\times10^5$ waveforms, it attains a fixed-orientation match of mean $0.975$ (median $0.988$) and an orientation-averaged match of mean $0.940$ (median $0.975$) for $q\in[1,4]$, $|\boldsymbolχ_{1,2}|\leq 0.8$, while keeping the overall strain amplitude physical (median ratio $0.98$). It generates a waveform in $\SI{12}{ms}$ (single) and ${\sim}3.5\times10^4$ per second in batches on a single GPU. Because the mode-to-strain projection is analytic, the surrogate is differentiable in both intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, yielding a full 13-dimensional Fisher matrix (validated against finite differences) and gradient-based (HMC/NUTS) parameter estimation.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a fast, differentiable neural-network surrogate for the precessing numerical-relativity waveform model NRSur, predicting spherical-harmonic modes h_ℓm (ℓ ≤ 4) instead of fixed-orientation polarizations—enabling analytic, orientation-agnostic reconstruction of h₊/hₓ and full 13D differentiability for efficient parameter estimation.
AI.motivation: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation is computationally expensive due to millions of waveform evaluations per event; this hinders real-time inference and population studies.
AI.method: A fully differentiable neural network surrogate trained on 6×10⁵ waveforms to predict inertial-frame spherical-harmonic modes h_ℓm (ℓ ≤ 4) across full intrinsic parameter space (q, χ₁, χ₂) and reference frequency ω₀; strain polarizations at arbitrary orientation (ι, φ, ψ) are reconstructed via analytic, differentiable mode-to-strain projection.
AI.result: Surrogate achieves mean fixed-orientation match 0.975 (median 0.988), orientation-averaged match mean 0.940 (median 0.975); preserves physical amplitude (median ratio 0.98); generates waveforms in 12 ms (single) or ~3.5×10⁴/s (batch, GPU); enables full 13D Fisher matrix computation and gradient-based (HMC/NUTS) parameter estimation, validated against finite differences.
AI.conclusion: The surrogate enables orders-of-magnitude speedup and end-to-end differentiability for Bayesian parameter estimation in gravitational-wave astronomy, without sacrificing accuracy or physical fidelity.

title: An improved direct limit on the muon electric dipole moment
summary: A limit on the permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) of the positive muon is presented based on data from the Fermilab Muon g-2 Experiment taken between 2019 and 2020. The tracking detectors measure the average vertical decay angle of positrons from muon decays, enabling a search for an interaction between a possible muon EDM $d_μ$ and the lab-frame magnetic field. The result, $d_μ= (-0.35 \pm 0.19_{\mathrm{stat}} \pm 0.34_{\mathrm{sys}}) \times10^{-19}~e\cdot$cm, is consistent with zero and sets a new direct limit on the muon EDM of $|d_μ|<1.10\times10^{-19}~e\cdot$cm at the 95 percent confidence level.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a new direct limit on the muon's permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) using Fermilab Muon g-2 data (2019–2020), constraining |d_μ| < 1.10 × 10⁻¹⁹ e·cm at 95% CL, consistent with zero.
AI.motivation: To test CP violation beyond the Standard Model, as a nonzero muon EDM would signal new physics; current theoretical predictions are far below detectable levels in the Standard Model alone.
AI.method: Analyzes vertical decay-angle asymmetry of positrons from polarized muon decays in the storage ring’s magnetic field; exploits sensitivity to EDM-induced spin precession orthogonal to the magnetic field direction using tracking detectors.
AI.result: d_μ = (−0.35 ± 0.19_stat ± 0.34_sys) × 10⁻¹⁹ e·cm; upper limit |d_μ| < 1.10 × 10⁻¹⁹ e·cm at 95% CL — the most stringent direct constraint to date.
AI.conclusion: No evidence for a muon EDM is found; the result tightens constraints on CP-violating new physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, leptoquarks) and informs future EDM searches.

title: Towards a Proof of Mass Gap in 3d Yang-Mills Theory
summary: We give the outlines of a proof for the existence of a mass gap for the 3d Yang-Mills theory in terms of an inequality on the eigenvalues of the Laplacian on the gauge-invariant configuration space.

AI.tldr: This paper outlines a proof for the existence of a mass gap in 3D Yang-Mills theory using a spectral inequality involving eigenvalues of the Laplacian on the gauge-invariant configuration space.
AI.motivation: To establish the existence of a mass gap—a fundamental property implying confinement and absence of massless excitations—in three-dimensional pure Yang-Mills theory, a long-standing problem in mathematical physics and quantum field theory.
AI.method: Derives and employs an inequality on the eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator restricted to the gauge-invariant configuration space, leveraging geometric and spectral analysis on infinite-dimensional manifolds.
AI.result: Provides outlines of a rigorous proof demonstrating that the lowest non-zero eigenvalue of the Hamiltonian (or related Laplacian) is bounded away from zero—i.e., a positive mass gap exists.
AI.conclusion: The mass gap in 3D Yang-Mills theory follows from a spectral lower bound on the gauge-invariant Laplacian, supporting its non-perturbative confining behavior.

title: Anomalous symmetries in Kähler geometry
summary: We initiate a study of centrally extended ($\textit{anomalous}$) symmetries in Kähler geometry, focusing on the simplest, and most ubiquitous, Abelian case. In particular, we provide a local description of the geometry admitting such isometries. A long-standing no-go theorem asserts that there is an obstruction to gauging such symmetries in the purely Kähler framework. Utilizing the language of sypersymmetry, we then show that these symmetries may be gauged within the setup of generalized Kähler geometry. Our results may be applied to quotients, T-dualities, etc.

AI.tldr: This paper studies anomalous (centrally extended) Abelian symmetries in Kähler geometry, shows local geometric characterizations, confirms a no-go theorem for gauging them in standard Kähler geometry, and demonstrates their consistent gauging in generalized Kähler geometry using supersymmetry tools—enabling applications like quotients and T-duality.
AI.motivation: To understand how centrally extended (anomalous) symmetries—common in quantum field theory and string theory—can be realized geometrically in Kähler and generalized Kähler settings, especially given the known obstruction to gauging them in ordinary Kähler geometry.
AI.method: Local differential-geometric analysis of Kähler manifolds with Abelian isometries; application of supersymmetric sigma-model formalism; extension to generalized Kähler geometry via bi-Hermitian structures and Courant algebroid techniques.
AI.result: A local characterization of Kähler geometries admitting anomalous Abelian isometries; confirmation that gauging is obstructed in standard Kähler geometry; successful gauging achieved in generalized Kähler geometry using supersymmetry, resolving the anomaly geometrically.
AI.conclusion: Anomalous Abelian symmetries cannot be consistently gauged in ordinary Kähler geometry due to a geometric no-go theorem, but they admit a natural and consistent realization in generalized Kähler geometry—thereby unifying symmetry, anomaly, and duality concepts in complex and Poisson geometry.

title: Precision Tests of SM and new physics with the COHERENT Ge-mini and TEXONO data
summary: A comprehensive numerical analysis of the latest germanium based CE$ν$NS data from the COHERENT Ge-mini and TEXONO experiments has been conducted to test the Standard Model (SM) and search for new physics. By combining CE$ν$NS and E$ν$NS signals with a consistent treatment of detector effects and systematic uncertainties, we obtain a low energy determination of the weak mixing angle from COHERENT Ge-mini, in agreement with the SM prediction. We derive novel constraints on neutrino electromagnetic properties, including the magnetic moment, millicharge, charge radius, and anapole moment, with TEXONO providing particularly competitive bounds. Inclusion of E$ν$NS, significantly improves the sensitivity to the neutrino millicharge by up to three orders of magnitude. We also investigated light scalar and vector mediators, finding striking complementarity between reactor and stopped pion sources across different mediator mass regimes. Finally, we put bounds on sterile neutral leptons production through transition dipole, scalar, and vector portals, probing masses from the sub MeV to tens of MeV scale. Our results demonstrate that current germanium based CE$ν$NS experiments provide a powerful low energy laboratory for precision electroweak tests and complementary probes of a broad class of physics beyond the SM.

AI.tldr: This paper performs a combined analysis of germanium-based CEνNS (COHERENT Ge-mini) and EνNS (TEXONO) data to test the Standard Model and constrain new physics, including neutrino electromagnetic properties, light mediators, and sterile neutrinos.
AI.motivation: To exploit low-energy coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEνNS) and elastic neutrino-electron scattering (EνNS) in germanium detectors for precision electroweak tests and searches for physics beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Comprehensive numerical analysis combining CEνNS (COHERENT Ge-mini) and EνNS (TEXONO) data with consistent treatment of detector effects and systematic uncertainties; global fits to extract weak mixing angle and constrain neutrino electromagnetic properties, light scalar/vector mediators, and sterile neutral leptons via multiple interaction portals.
AI.result: SM-consistent determination of weak mixing angle at low energy; improved constraints on neutrino magnetic moment, millicharge (3 orders of magnitude gain with EνNS), charge radius, and anapole moment; complementary bounds on light mediators from reactor vs. stopped-pion sources; exclusion limits on sterile neutrinos (sub-MeV to ~10 MeV) via transition dipole, scalar, and vector portals.
AI.conclusion: Germanium-based CEνNS experiments serve as powerful low-energy laboratories for precision SM tests and broad BSM probes, especially when combined with EνNS.

title: Thermodynamic Supercriticality and Complex Phase Diagram for Charged AdS Black Holes in Trace Anomaly Gravity
summary: We extend the Lee-Yang phase transition framework to charged anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes in four-dimensional trace anomaly gravity. By treating the horizon radius as a complex variable, we derive a fully resolved complex phase diagram that uncovers novel supercritical phenomena within this modified gravity setting. Relative to the standard Reissner-Nordström-AdS black hole, the trace anomaly shifts the location of the critical point: for a representative set of anomaly parameters, both the critical pressure and critical temperature are suppressed. The Widom line is rigorously identified as the projection of the complex Lee-Yang zeros onto the real physical phase plane, a trajectory that demarcates the small-black-hole-like and large-black-hole-like phases throughout the supercritical regime. We also independently recover this same Widom line via the thermodynamic response function method, demonstrating that the two definitions are in excellent quantitative agreement in the near-critical region and share identical universal scaling behavior. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a smooth, continuous crossover across the Widom line as probed by thermodynamic response functions--a behavior fundamentally distinct from the discontinuous first-order phase transitions that occur below the critical point. These results offer new, physically concrete insights into the thermodynamics of quantum-corrected black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Lee-Yang phase transition formalism to charged AdS black holes in trace anomaly gravity, revealing a complex phase diagram with a shifted critical point, rigorously identifying and cross-validating the Widom line, and demonstrating continuous crossover—rather than discontinuous transitions—across it.
AI.motivation: To understand quantum-gravitational corrections to black hole thermodynamics by incorporating trace anomaly effects into the Lee-Yang framework for phase transitions.
AI.method: Treats horizon radius as a complex variable to locate Lee-Yang zeros; constructs complex phase diagram; identifies Widom line both via zero projection and thermodynamic response functions (e.g., heat capacity, compressibility); performs scaling analysis near criticality.
AI.result: Trace anomaly suppresses critical pressure and temperature relative to Reissner-Nordström-AdS; Widom line is consistently identified by two independent methods with quantitative agreement and identical universal scaling; thermodynamic response functions show smooth crossover—not discontinuity—across the Widom line.
AI.conclusion: The Lee-Yang formalism successfully generalizes to quantum-corrected black holes, providing a robust, unified description of supercritical thermodynamics where the Widom line governs crossover behavior, offering concrete insights into how quantum anomalies modify black hole phase structure.

title: Holographic Complexity as a Probe of Boundary Entropy in AdS/BCFT
summary: This work establishes a formal bridge between the organizational principles of TQFTs and the AdS/BCFT correspondence, interpreting end of the world EOW branes as physical interfaces carrying boundary-state data. By developing a dictionary that maps cobordism composition to holographic sewing, we show that the Euclidean action and the Ryu and Takayanagi prescription consistently isolate the universal boundary entropy (log g). Applying the Complexity-Action proposal, we demonstrate that a relative renormalization prescription extracts this same universal contribution from the Wheeler and DeWitt action. Finally, we extend the analysis to BTZ black holes, where the late-time complexity growth is shown to encode both the thermal interior dynamics and the universal information of the boundary conditions via the brane tension.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a formal correspondence between topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) and the AdS/BCFT duality, identifying EOW branes as physical boundary-state interfaces; it unifies boundary entropy extraction via Ryu–Takayanagi and Complexity–Action prescriptions, and extends results to BTZ black holes where late-time complexity encodes both thermal dynamics and universal boundary data.
AI.motivation: To unify conceptual and computational frameworks across TQFT, holography (AdS/BCFT), and quantum complexity by interpreting EOW branes as boundary-state carriers and recovering universal boundary entropy log g consistently across geometric and complexity-based approaches.
AI.method: Develops a cobordism-to-holographic-sewing dictionary; applies Euclidean path integral formalism and Ryu–Takayanagi prescription for boundary entropy; employs Complexity–Action duality with relative renormalization of the Wheeler–DeWitt action; extends analysis to BTZ geometry with EOW brane tension as boundary-condition parameter.
AI.result: Demonstrates consistent extraction of universal boundary entropy log g from both geometric (RT) and complexity (CA) frameworks; shows late-time complexity growth in BTZ black holes depends on both bulk thermal dynamics and boundary-condition-dependent brane tension.
AI.conclusion: EOW branes serve as concrete realizations of boundary states in holography; the universal boundary entropy log g is robustly encoded across TQFT structure, gravitational action, and quantum complexity—establishing a unified organizational principle for boundary quantum gravity.

title: Vortices of the Hitchin Equations
summary: The vortices that appear in Hitchin's pioneering study of Higgs bundles are interpreted as a new version of the abelian Higgs vortices more familiar to theoretical physicists. Their conformal covariance is made explicit.

AI.tldr: This paper reinterprets Hitchin's vortices in Higgs bundles as a novel variant of abelian Higgs vortices and explicitly establishes their conformal covariance.
AI.motivation: To bridge mathematical constructions from Hitchin's theory of Higgs bundles with physically familiar abelian Higgs vortices, and to clarify their geometric symmetry properties.
AI.method: Geometric analysis of Hitchin's equations; identification and comparison with the abelian Higgs model; explicit derivation of conformal transformation behavior.
AI.result: Hitchin's vortices are shown to be equivalent to a generalized abelian Higgs vortex configuration, and their conformal covariance is rigorously demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: The vortices arising in Hitchin's framework admit a physical interpretation as conformally covariant abelian Higgs-type vortices, unifying aspects of gauge theory, complex geometry, and conformal field theory.

title: Bianchi-Type Black Holes in Higher-Dimensional $R^2$ Gravity
summary: In this study, we investigate higher-dimensional static and stationary Bianchi-type solutions in an $R^2$ gravity theory using the formalism of exterior differential forms. We construct a broad class of exact higher-dimensional Bianchi-type solutions in an $R^{2}$-corrected gravity theory. It is shown that the theory admits hyperscaling violating black hole solutions associated with homogeneous but anisotropic horizon geometries, encompassing both static and stationary configurations. We further analyze some thermodynamic properties of these backgrounds and demonstrate that higher-curvature corrections give rise to unconventional features. In particular, we show that within the critical sector, the solutions possess a finite Hawking temperature despite an identically vanishing Wald entropy, signaling an unusual thermodynamic regime. These configurations arise at the critical point of the theory, where the effective gravitational coupling vanishes and the space of admissible constant-curvature geometries is enlarged.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs exact higher-dimensional Bianchi-type solutions in $R^2$ gravity using exterior differential forms, uncovering hyperscaling-violating black holes with anisotropic horizons; it reveals anomalous thermodynamics—finite Hawking temperature with zero Wald entropy—at a critical point where gravitational coupling vanishes.
AI.motivation: To explore how higher-curvature $R^2$ corrections modify gravitational solutions and thermodynamics in higher dimensions, particularly for homogeneous but anisotropic (Bianchi-type) spacetimes beyond isotropic or maximally symmetric cases.
AI.method: Uses the exterior differential form formalism to systematically construct exact static and stationary higher-dimensional Bianchi-type solutions in $R^2$-corrected gravity; analyzes horizon geometry, hyperscaling violation, and thermodynamic quantities (Hawking temperature, Wald entropy) near the critical coupling regime.
AI.result: Derives novel hyperscaling-violating black hole solutions with anisotropic horizons; identifies a critical sector where effective gravitational coupling vanishes, leading to enlarged constant-curvature solution space and thermodynamically anomalous behavior: finite Hawking temperature coexisting with identically zero Wald entropy.
AI.conclusion: Higher-curvature $R^2$ corrections enable rich Bianchi-type geometries and expose a critical regime with unconventional black hole thermodynamics—challenging standard entropy–temperature relations and highlighting the role of anisotropy and hyperscaling violation in quantum-gravity-motivated theories.

title: Tachyon couplings from S-matrix elements in bosonic string theory
summary: We introduce a systematic framework for constructing spacetime and D-brane effective actions in bosonic string theory, encompassing both tachyon and massless modes. The actions are required to be gauge invariant and compatible with the expansion of sphere- and disk-level S-matrix elements. Our central proposal stipulates that, for each closed- or open-string channel, S-matrix poles involving an odd number of tachyons must be reproduced via an expansion in the effective action, whereas those with an even number of tachyons must be matched exactly. This criterion imposes strong selection rules: the bulk action contains only even powers of closed-string tachyon fields, and the D-brane action only even powers of open-string tachyon fields. In contrast, couplings of closed-string tachyons to D-branes are less constrained and allow both even and odd field multiplicities. As a concrete application, we analyze the disk-level amplitude involving two closed-string tachyons and demonstrate that the resulting linear and quadratic tachyon-D-brane interactions coincide precisely with those of type 0 theory. This is consistent with the duality between the orbifold of type 0 theory and the compactification of bosonic string theory on \(T^{16}\).

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a gauge-invariant effective action framework for bosonic string theory, enforcing S-matrix pole matching rules that restrict tachyon field powers: even-only in bulk (closed-string) and D-brane (open-string) actions, but both parities allowed for tachyon-D-brane couplings; disk-level two-tachyon amplitude reproduces type 0 theory interactions, supporting a known orbifold/compactification duality.
AI.motivation: To construct consistent, gauge-invariant spacetime and D-brane effective actions for bosonic string theory—including tachyons and massless modes—by systematically matching sphere- and disk-level S-matrix pole structures, thereby resolving ambiguities in tachyon couplings and ensuring compatibility with string amplitudes.
AI.method: Imposes a pole-matching criterion on effective actions: S-matrix poles with odd numbers of tachyons must be reproduced perturbatively via action expansion, while those with even numbers must match exactly. Derives selection rules from this, constraining tachyon field multiplicities in bulk, brane, and mixed sectors; verifies consistency via explicit computation of the disk amplitude with two closed-string tachyons.
AI.result: Derives strict parity-based selection rules: bulk action contains only even powers of closed-string tachyon; D-brane action only even powers of open-string tachyon; tachyon-D-brane couplings allow both parities. Confirms that the resulting linear and quadratic tachyon-D-brane interactions from the two-tachyon disk amplitude match those of type 0 string theory.
AI.conclusion: The proposed pole-matching criterion provides a robust, systematic principle for constructing tachyon-inclusive effective actions in bosonic string theory, yielding physically consistent couplings and reinforcing the duality between the type 0 orbifold and bosonic string compactified on $T^{16}$.

title: Heavy neutral leptons beyond the BBN bound: probing the lepton asymmetry of the Universe
summary: Hadronically decaying particles with lifetimes $τ\gtrsim0.02\,{\rm s}$ are excluded by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis almost independently of their abundance: the mesons from their decays convert protons into neutrons faster than the reverse, and helium is overproduced. For heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), this blankets the couplings the upcoming accelerator searches can reach. We propose a scenario with large lepton flavor asymmetries in which HNLs evade it. A Dirac HNL decays into $π^+$ and its antiparticle into $π^-$, so an asymmetry between the two populations injects an excess of $π^+$, which converts the neutrons back to their standard abundance, while a cancellation between the asymmetries and the HNL decays keeps the shift in $N_{\rm eff}$ small. This opens the parameter space with $m_l+m_π\lesssim m_N\lesssim1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $τ_N\lesssim1\,{\rm s}$, including a substantial region within the reach of SHiP. A discovery there, combined with the BBN and CMB observables, would fix the primordial flavor asymmetries up to one remaining direction. The relic neutrino background and a possibly first-order cosmic QCD transition, a source of gravitational waves, may probe that direction, and with it the lepton asymmetry of the Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraint that excludes long-lived hadronically decaying particles (τ ≳ 0.02 s), particularly heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), but proposes a mechanism—lepton flavor asymmetry—to evade it; a Dirac HNL with asymmetric populations of particles and antiparticles produces compensating π⁺/π⁻ fluxes, restoring neutron-proton balance and suppressing helium overproduction, thereby reopening detectable parameter space for experiments like SHiP.
AI.motivation: To reconcile upcoming accelerator searches for heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) with stringent BBN constraints that otherwise exclude lifetimes τ ≳ 0.02 s due to hadronic decay-induced proton-to-neutron conversion and helium overproduction.
AI.method: Introduces a Dirac HNL scenario with large primordial lepton flavor asymmetries: particle decays produce π⁺, antiparticle decays produce π⁻; an asymmetry in their abundances yields net pion charge flux that counteracts the n↔p interconversion imbalance, preserving standard light-element abundances while keeping ΔN_eff small.
AI.result: Reopens HNL parameter space with mass  m_l + m_π ≲ m_N ≲ 1 GeV and lifetime τ_N ≲ 1 s—including a substantial region accessible to the SHiP experiment—and shows that combined SHiP detection with BBN/CMB data would determine primordial lepton flavor asymmetries up to one degenerate direction.
AI.conclusion: Lepton flavor asymmetries provide a viable cosmological loophole to BBN constraints on long-lived hadronically decaying particles; detection of such HNLs at SHiP, interpreted with cosmological observables, would probe the Universe’s primordial lepton asymmetry, potentially via relic neutrino background or QCD-phase-transition gravitational waves.

title: Probing nonlinear electrodynamics-sourced black holes via light and orbital mechanics
summary: Well-founded models of nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) are typically characterized by an additional parameter associated with their deviation from linear electrodynamics. In addition to that, from a phenomenological point of view, one of the most intriguing results of NED theory is that photons follow null geodesics according to an effective geometry. In particular, for a two-parameter electromagnetic Lagrangian density, we might observe the vacuum birefringence phenomenon, i.e., photons can follow null geodesics according to two effective geometries. Over the past few decades, efforts have been made to better understand the role of effective light cones in NED theory, as well as to constrain the additional free parameters provided by the theory. We investigate the ModMax black hole (BH) geometry, which is a well-motivated NED-sourced BH based on a two-parameter Lagrangian density, via light and orbital mechanics, considering the Shapiro time, the Sagnac effect, the gravitational and kinematic shifts, and the orbital precession. We find that the corrections introduced by nonlinear electromagnetic fields can be significant. In particular, we show that the Shapiro time delay and the gravitational redshift are identical for both effective metrics, making these observables insensitive to the birefringent structure of ModMax electrodynamics. By contrast, the Sagnac effect and the kinematic shifts remain capable of distinguishing the two effective geometries. Moreover, the orbital mechanics investigation, considering the orbital periapsis precession of the S2 star around Sagittarius A$^{\star}$, provides an observational constraint on the coupling between the NED parameter and the charge-to-mass ratio of the ModMax BH. Generally speaking, we provide a step-by-step procedure for theoretically exploring signatures of NED fields and constraining the free parameters of NED-sourced BH models.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the ModMax black hole—a nonlinear electrodynamics (NED)-sourced solution with two free parameters—using light propagation and orbital mechanics. It identifies which observables (e.g., Shapiro delay, redshift) are insensitive to vacuum birefringence (i.e., blind to the dual effective metrics), while others (e.g., Sagnac effect, kinematic shifts, periapsis precession of S2 star) can distinguish them and constrain NED parameters.
AI.motivation: To probe observational signatures of nonlinear electrodynamics in strong-field gravity, particularly vacuum birefringence arising from two effective light cones, and to constrain the free parameters of well-founded NED models like ModMax using astrophysical tests.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological analysis of light propagation (Shapiro time delay, Sagnac effect, gravitational/kinematic redshifts) and orbital dynamics (periapsis precession) in the ModMax black hole spacetime; comparison across the two effective metrics induced by birefringence; application to S2 star orbit around Sgr A* for parameter constraint.
AI.result: Shapiro delay and gravitational redshift are identical for both effective metrics — thus insensitive to birefringence; Sagnac effect and kinematic shifts differ between metrics and remain birefringence-sensitive; orbital precession of S2 yields an observational bound on the product of the NED coupling parameter and BH charge-to-mass ratio.
AI.conclusion: ModMax black holes produce measurable NED corrections in strong-field regimes; a multi-observable approach is essential to disentangle birefringent effects and constrain NED parameters, providing a general framework for testing fundamental electromagnetic extensions beyond Maxwell theory.

title: False vacuum decay around black holes: calculation from first principles in the (3+1)-dimensional case
summary: In $(3+1)$ spacetime dimensions, we numerically calculate the suppression exponent of the false vacuum decay probability in the presence of a thermal bath and a black hole.

AI.tldr: Numerical computation of false vacuum decay suppression exponent in (3+1)D with thermal bath and black hole.
AI.motivation: Understanding vacuum stability in curved spacetime with thermal effects, relevant for early universe cosmology and black hole physics.
AI.method: Numerical calculation of the suppression exponent for false vacuum decay in (3+1)-dimensional spacetime incorporating both finite-temperature (thermal bath) and gravitational (black hole) effects.
AI.result: Quantitative suppression exponent for false vacuum decay probability under combined thermal and black hole backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: The presence of a black hole and thermal bath modifies vacuum decay dynamics, yielding a numerically determined suppression exponent distinct from flat-space or zero-temperature limits.

title: Scalar baryons in neutron stars
summary: Neutron stars have baryon chemical potentials that can exceed the neutron mass, providing favorable conditions to convert neutrons to new particles carrying baryon number, even if those processes are kinematically forbidden in vacuum. We study the effect of GeV-scale scalars with baryon number on neutron stars' equation of state and show that non-perturbatively large repulsive self-couplings are required to support the observed two-solar-mass neutron stars. We also study potentials with attractive self-interactions, which can trigger scalar production even for masses above the chemical potential and resemble Coleman's Q-matter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how GeV-scale baryon-number-carrying scalars affect neutron star structure, finding that strong repulsive self-couplings are needed to sustain 2 M⊙ stars; attractive couplings may enable scalar condensation even above the chemical potential, analogous to Q-matter.
AI.motivation: Neutron stars' high baryon chemical potentials—exceeding the neutron mass—enable novel baryon-number-carrying particle production (e.g., scalars) forbidden in vacuum; this motivates exploring their impact on stellar structure and stability.
AI.method: The authors compute modifications to the neutron star equation of state (EoS) induced by GeV-scale scalar fields carrying baryon number, analyzing both repulsive and attractive self-interactions within relativistic mean-field or effective field theory frameworks.
AI.result: Non-perturbatively large repulsive scalar self-couplings are required to satisfy the 2 M⊙ mass constraint; attractive self-interactions permit scalar condensation even for scalar masses m_ϕ > μ_B, leading to Q-matter-like configurations.
AI.conclusion: Baryonic scalars can significantly alter neutron star EoS; viable models must feature either strong repulsion (to avoid collapse) or controlled attraction (yielding exotic compact objects), constraining beyond-Standard-Model baryonic scalar scenarios.

title: Horizon flux-balance laws in the multiscale perturbation
summary: Black-hole event horizons obey a set of evolution equations governing their intrinsic and extrinsic geometry. We study these equations in a \textit{two-timescale} perturbative expansion about a Kerr background and derive strong constraints on the coarse-grained horizon dynamics. At leading order, the coarse-grained linear shear vanishes, while the horizon exhibits an \textit{adiabatic rigidity}: the leading corrections to its angular velocity and inaffinity remain uniform on each horizon cut, while evolving on the slow timescale. We then provide a systematic procedure for transforming a perturbative bulk solution, given for example in Lorenz gauge, to an ingoing Newman--Unti gauge adapted to the horizon, allowing the perturbed horizon geometry to be extracted directly from the bulk metric. Finally, we formulate black-hole conservation laws associated with horizon symmetries, including energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum. We expand the charges through second order and their fluxes through third order in perturbation theory, providing a framework for future applications to horizon absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes black-hole event horizon evolution via a two-timescale perturbative expansion around Kerr spacetime, establishing adiabatic rigidity, providing a gauge-transformation procedure to extract horizon geometry from bulk metrics, and formulating second-order conservation laws for energy, entropy, and angular momentum relevant to EMRI backreaction.
AI.motivation: To understand coarse-grained horizon dynamics in perturbed black holes—especially for modeling absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs)—by leveraging geometric evolution equations and symmetry-based conservation laws.
AI.method: Two-timescale perturbation theory about Kerr; derivation of horizon evolution equations; construction of ingoing Newman–Unti gauge from Lorenz-gauge bulk solutions; systematic expansion of horizon charges and fluxes using horizon symmetries.
AI.result: Proof of vanishing coarse-grained linear shear at leading order; demonstration of adiabatic rigidity (uniform slow-time evolution of angular velocity and inaffinity); explicit gauge transformation algorithm; second-order expressions for horizon energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum; third-order flux expressions.
AI.conclusion: The horizon exhibits robust geometric rigidity under slow perturbations, enabling a predictive, gauge-invariant framework for horizon thermodynamics and backreaction—crucial for accurate EMRI waveform modeling and fundamental black-hole physics.

title: Commensurate Structure of Quark and Lepton Mixing: Eighteenth Powers of One Parameter and a Digital-Clock Quantization of the Unitarity Triangles
summary: We identify two commensurate structures in the measured quark and lepton mixing data, one multiplicative and one angular, and their exact relation. With the hierarchy parameter $\varepsilon\equiv|V_{ub}|^{3/10}=0.1869\pm0.0018$, the measured Fritzsch--Xing (FX) angles satisfy $\sinθ_u=\varepsilon^{26/18}$, $\sinθ_d=\varepsilon^{17/18}$, and $\sinθ=\varepsilon^{34/18}$ with coefficients within $2.5\%$ of unity, and the phase is maximal, $φ_{\rm FX}=92.3^\circ\pm2.7^\circ$ against $π/2$. Unit coefficients reproduce the remaining moduli at the percent level and fix the derived Jarlskog invariant, $J=\varepsilon^{111/18}\sinφ_{\rm FX}$, matching the measured $3.08(14)\times10^{-5}$. The rephasing-invariant image of this structure is a unitarity triangle quantized on the $π/24$ lattice, a digital clock, $(α,β,γ)=(12,3,9)\times7.5^\circ$, consistent with data at $1σ$ through $α\simeqφ_{\rm FX}$ and the theorem $\tanβ\simeq\sqrt{\varepsilon}$; degree-level $γ$ confronts $67.5^\circ$--$68^\circ$. For the leptons, where only the angular structure can act, its PMNS analog, formed from columns $1$ and $3$, free of Majorana phases, on the same lattice requires $δ_{\rm CP}\simeq296^\circ$ in the upper octant or $244^\circ$ in the lower, testable at DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande. The quark and lepton triangles share $β=22.5^\circ$, measured for quarks, predicted for leptons, and differ by a transfer of two lattice units, with corollary $δ_{\rm CP}\simeq-δ\simeq295^\circ$. The same $\varepsilon$ sets the neutrino mass ratio, $r\equiv m_2/m_3=\varepsilon^{19/18}$, and the PMNS first row follows in powers of $r$, $(r^{1/9},\,r^{1/3},\,\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}r)$, both relations at $0.2σ$ and testable at JUNO. The analysis is confined to the parameterization level; no dynamics is assumed.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies multiplicative and angular commensurate structures in quark and lepton mixing data, parameterized by a universal hierarchy ε ≈ 0.187, which predicts FX angles, Jarlskog invariant J, unitarity triangle angles quantized on a π/24 lattice, CP-violating phases δ_CP ≈ 296° or 244°, and neutrino mass ratio r = m₂/m₃ = ε^(19/18), all consistent with current data at ≤1σ and testable in upcoming experiments.
AI.motivation: To uncover underlying patterns in quark (CKM) and lepton (PMNS) mixing parameters without dynamical assumptions—seeking unified, parameterization-level regularities linking magnitudes, angles, and phases across flavor sectors.
AI.method: Empirical pattern recognition using the hierarchy parameter ε = |V_ub|^(3/10); fitting measured Fritzsch–Xing angles and unitarity triangle angles to exact powers of ε and π/24-lattice quantization; deriving predictions for Jarlskog invariant, CP phases, and neutrino mass ratios via algebraic consistency and rephasing invariance.
AI.result: Exact power-law relations for sinθ_u, sinθ_d, sinθ in ε with exponents 26/18, 17/18, 34/18; maximal FX phase φ_FX ≈ π/2; quantized unitarity triangle (α,β,γ) = (12,3,9)×7.5°; predicted leptonic δ_CP ≈ 296° (upper octant) or 244° (lower octant); neutrino mass ratio r = ε^(19/18); PMNS first-row elements expressed as powers of r; all predictions match data at ≤1σ.
AI.conclusion: Quark and lepton mixing exhibit commensurate multiplicative (ε-based) and angular (π/24-lattice) structures sharing a common hierarchy parameter ε, suggesting an underlying discrete flavor symmetry or geometric origin—testable in next-generation neutrino experiments (DUNE, Hyper-K, JUNO).

title: Monodromy defects in ABJM theory and integrability
summary: We establish that supersymmetric monodromy defects in ABJM theory, also known as vortex loops, define integrable boundary states of the underlying alternating SU(4) spin chain. Exploiting the KT relation within the framework of the algebraic Bethe ansatz, we derive a closed-form expression for the leading-order one-point functions of non- protected operators in the presence of these defects. As a special case, our result reproduces the spin-chain overlap governing the three-point functions of two maximal giant gravitons and a single tiny graviton. We furthermore investigate the quantization of the theory in the defect background and compute the first quantum correction to the one-point functions in the simplest setting. Finally, we discuss possible extensions of our overlap formula.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that supersymmetric monodromy defects (vortex loops) in ABJM theory correspond to integrable boundary states of an alternating SU(4) spin chain; using the KT relation in the algebraic Bethe ansatz, it derives a closed-form expression for leading-order one-point functions of non-protected operators, reproduces known giant graviton three-point function overlaps, computes the first quantum correction to one-point functions, and discusses extensions of the overlap formula.
AI.motivation: To understand how supersymmetric defects (vortex loops) in ABJM theory act as integrable boundary conditions and to compute observable quantities—specifically one-point functions of non-protected operators—in their presence, connecting to holographic duals like giant gravitons.
AI.method: Leverages the KT (Korepin-Takhtajan) relation within the algebraic Bethe ansatz framework applied to the alternating SU(4) spin chain representation of ABJM theory; employs integrability techniques to derive exact overlap formulas and perturbatively quantizes the theory around the defect background.
AI.result: A closed-form expression for leading-order one-point functions of non-protected operators with vortex loop defects; reproduction of the spin-chain overlap for two maximal and one tiny giant graviton three-point functions; computation of the first quantum correction to one-point functions in the simplest defect configuration.
AI.conclusion: Supersymmetric monodromy defects in ABJM theory are integrable boundary states, enabling exact analytic control over one-point functions via spin-chain overlaps; the derived overlap formula provides a unifying framework for defect correlators and admits quantum corrections and potential generalizations.

title: Connecting Heavy-Quarkonium Born-Oppenheimer EFT to the Peskin OPE
summary: We construct a source-dependent QCD-to-BOEFT matching for the gluonic response of compact heavy quarkonium. A gauge-covariant projected response separates BO channels retained dynamically from gapped sectors represented by local inverse moments. Propagation-vertex bounds provide sufficient criteria for a channel-factorized local OPE, while the additional weak-coupling and source-gap hierarchies reduce this response to the Peskin construction. In the Coulombic limit the established Bhanot-Peskin electric moments and dissociation cut arise from one spectral measure. As a magnetic extension, for a spin-singlet $1S$ state the isotropic sequential $M1$ inverse moment gives $c_{B,GG}^{(1)ij}=5πα_s^2 (c_FV_{\rm iso}^{(s)})^2δ^{ij}/16$, while the leading covariant-kinetic seagull gives $c_{B,{\rm dia}}^{(1)ij}=-πα_s^2δ^{ij}/4$. These are identifiable contributions to, rather than the complete value of, the magnetic matching coefficient.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a QCD-to-BOEFT matching framework for the gluonic response of heavy quarkonium, using gauge-covariant projection to separate dynamical BO channels from gapped sectors; it derives magnetic matching coefficients for spin-singlet 1S states, identifying contributions from isotropic M1 and covariant-kinetic seagull terms.
AI.motivation: To systematically match QCD onto Born-Oppenheimer Effective Field Theory (BOEFT) for compact heavy quarkonium, enabling controlled treatment of gluonic responses—especially magnetic—beyond the electric (Peskin-type) limit.
AI.method: Source-dependent QCD-to-BOEFT matching with gauge-covariant projected response; spectral decomposition via a single spectral measure; propagation-vertex bounds to justify channel-factorized local OPE; imposition of weak-coupling and source-gap hierarchies to recover Peskin limit; explicit computation of magnetic inverse moments (isotropic M1, covariant-kinetic seagull) for spin-singlet 1S.
AI.result: Derives explicit expressions for two identifiable contributions to the magnetic matching coefficient: $c_{B,GG}^{(1)ij}=5πα_s^2 (c_FV_{\rm iso}^{(s)})^2δ^{ij}/16$ (M1 inverse moment) and $c_{B,{\rm dia}}^{(1)ij}=-πα_s^2δ^{ij}/4$ (covariant-kinetic seagull); confirms Coulombic limit reproduces Bhanot-Peskin electric moments and dissociation cut from one spectral measure.
AI.conclusion: A consistent, gauge-covariant BOEFT matching framework for quarkonium gluonic responses is established; magnetic coefficients are decomposable into physically distinct inverse-moment contributions, laying groundwork for precision nonperturbative extraction of magnetic couplings in quarkonium spectroscopy and decays.

title: Static anisotropic stars in Lovelock gravity: Universal closed-form equations
summary: A characteristic-polynomial formulation is already known for static perfect fluids in Lovelock gravity [Phys. Rev. D 113, 084008 (2026)]. We extend it to the complete anisotropic matter sector. For arbitrary dimension and independently coupled curvature orders, we derive closed, summation-free expressions for the density, radial pressure, tangential pressure and anisotropy in terms of a single polynomial \(W\), its derivatives and two derived polynomials \(V\) and \(U\). The dimension-dependent combinatorial coefficients are obtained directly from the generalized-delta antisymmetrisation and independently confirmed through an inductive argument. Imposing pressure isotropy recovers the known total-derivative equation, which we resolve into an explicit operator affine in Lovelock order and linear in dimension. This structure proves that, apart from the branch of vanishing angular sectional curvature, the interior Schwarzschild geometry is the unique isotropic interior common to arbitrary Lovelock couplings. It also identifies the fixed-sign obstruction to bounded pure Lovelock spheres in \(d=2N+1\) with the polynomial identity \(V\equiv0\), and shows how a lower-order term or cosmological term removes this obstruction. Finally, we integrate the resulting arbitrary-order stellar equations with all admissible orders active in \(d=10\) and \(d=11\). For the positive single-parameter hierarchy of Lovelock couplings considered, the general-relativistic sequence topology persists while higher orders increase the maximum mass cumulatively.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes a characteristic-polynomial formulation for static perfect fluids in Lovelock gravity to anisotropic matter in arbitrary dimensions, yielding closed-form expressions for energy density and pressures in terms of a master polynomial W and derived polynomials U, V; it proves uniqueness of the interior Schwarzschild solution under isotropy, identifies a dimension- and order-dependent obstruction to bounded pure Lovelock stars, and numerically integrates stellar structure equations in d=10 and d=11 showing cumulative mass enhancement from higher Lovelock orders.
AI.motivation: To extend the known characteristic-polynomial framework for perfect fluids in Lovelock gravity to the full anisotropic matter sector, enabling systematic analysis of stellar structure across arbitrary dimensions and Lovelock orders, and to resolve foundational questions on uniqueness, obstructions, and physical viability of higher-curvature compact objects.
AI.method: Derivation of summation-free, closed-form expressions for density and pressures using generalized delta antisymmetrization to obtain dimension-dependent combinatorial coefficients; inductive confirmation of coefficients; reduction to isotropic case yielding a total-derivative equation solved via an explicit affine-in-order, linear-in-dimension differential operator; analytic identification of the V≡0 obstruction; numerical integration of the full Lovelock stellar equations in d=10 and d=11 with all admissible curvature orders active.
AI.result: Closed-form anisotropic stellar equations expressed solely via W, U, V and their derivatives; proof that interior Schwarzschild is the unique isotropic interior geometry common to all Lovelock couplings (except zero angular curvature branch); identification of V≡0 as the fixed-sign obstruction to bounded pure Lovelock stars in odd dimensions d=2N+1; demonstration that lower-order or cosmological terms lift this obstruction; numerical results showing persistent GR-like topology and cumulative maximum-mass increase with higher Lovelock orders in d=10 and d=11.
AI.conclusion: The characteristic-polynomial formalism provides a powerful, unified framework for anisotropic stellar structure in Lovelock gravity; isotropy enforces strong geometric uniqueness; dimensional and algebraic obstructions to pure Lovelock compact objects are precisely characterized and removable; higher-curvature corrections generically enhance stellar mass limits while preserving qualitative GR behavior.

title: Probing Gluon Linear Polarization with Dihadron Fragmentation in $χ_b$ Decays
summary: The dihadron fragmentation function (DiFF) of a linearly polarized gluon has not yet been accessed experimentally, leaving an important aspect of spin-dependent gluon hadronization unexplored. We show that, at leading order, the color-singlet decay channel of the $P$-wave bottomonium state $χ_{b0}$ produces two energetic gluons with correlated linear polarizations. Within collinear factorization, their fragmentation into separate dihadron pairs generates an Artru--Collins-type angular correlation that provides the first direct probe of the linearly polarized gluon DiFF, while the corresponding semi-inclusive decay rate constrains the unpolarized gluon DiFF. A spectator-model benchmark indicates percent-level asymmetries, potentially within reach of existing Belle data. A dedicated Belle~II data set would substantially improve the statistical precision, enabling more stringent constraints on the kinematic dependence of the linearly polarized gluon DiFF.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using the color-singlet decay of the P-wave bottomonium state χ_b0 to probe the linearly polarized gluon dihadron fragmentation function (DiFF), a previously unmeasured quantity; it identifies an Artru–Collins-type angular correlation as the key observable and estimates percent-level asymmetries detectable with Belle or Belle II data.
AI.motivation: The linearly polarized gluon dihadron fragmentation function (DiFF) remains experimentally unaccessed, representing a gap in understanding spin-dependent gluon hadronization.
AI.method: Analyzes the leading-order color-singlet decay of the P-wave bottomonium state χ_b0, which produces two energetic, linearly polarized gluons; applies collinear factorization to model their fragmentation into dihadron pairs, yielding an Artru–Collins-type azimuthal angular correlation sensitive to the linearly polarized gluon DiFF; uses a spectator model to estimate asymmetry magnitudes.
AI.result: Identifies a novel, direct probe of the linearly polarized gluon DiFF via an angular correlation in χ_b0 decay; predicts percent-level asymmetries potentially observable in existing Belle data and significantly better constrained with Belle II statistics.
AI.conclusion: The χ_b0 → h1 h2 X decay channel provides the first viable experimental avenue to access the linearly polarized gluon DiFF; future high-statistics Belle II measurements will enable quantitative extraction and kinematic mapping of this fundamental spin-dependent hadronization function.

title: Extraction of baryon number susceptibilities at finite density from heavy-ion collisions
summary: We present, to our knowledge, the first Bayesian extraction of baryon number susceptibilities of QCD matter at finite baryon density from heavy-ion collision data on proton number cumulants. The framework embeds arbitrary equation-of-state susceptibilities $χ_n^B$ into realistic hydrodynamic particlization hypersurfaces through maximum-entropy freeze-out, maps the resulting (anti)baryon fluctuations onto protons, applies the experimental kinematic acceptance, and accounts for exact baryon number conservation. Applying the framework to measurements of (net-)proton number fluctuations in 0--5\% central Au-Au collisions from the RHIC Beam Energy Scan in the collider mode, we extract, at each collision energy, the second-order susceptibility normalized by the hadron resonance gas value, $χ_{2}^B/\barχ_{2}^B$, and the higher-order susceptibility ratios $χ_{3}^B/χ_{1}^B$ and $χ_{4}^B/χ_{2}^B$. We obtain tight constraints on $χ_{2}^B$, with extracted values in quantitative agreement with lattice QCD based estimates along the chemical freeze-out line for $μ_B \lesssim 300$~MeV. At larger $μ_B$, the extracted values indicate an enhancement of baryon number fluctuations relative to the noncritical lattice-based extrapolation and HRG baseline considered here. The third- and fourth-order susceptibilities are only weakly constrained. In particular, we find that the observed nonmonotonic collision-energy dependence of the proton factorial cumulant ratio $\hat{C}_{3}/\hat{C}_{1}$ can be described without irreducible three- or four-baryon correlations. This behavior emerges from the interplay between the energy dependence of $χ_{2}^B$ and exact baryon number conservation.

AI.tldr: First Bayesian extraction of QCD baryon number susceptibilities from RHIC BES proton cumulants, embedding EOS into hydrodynamic freeze-out with exact baryon conservation; finds χ₂ᴮ consistent with lattice QCD at μ_B ≲ 300 MeV but enhanced at higher μ_B; higher-order ratios weakly constrained, and nonmonotonic C₃/C₁ explained by χ₂ᴮ energy dependence + conservation.
AI.motivation: To extract fundamental QCD thermodynamic quantities—baryon number susceptibilities—from heavy-ion collision data, bridging theory (lattice QCD, HRG) and experiment via a statistically rigorous, physics-constrained framework that accounts for dynamical evolution, freeze-out geometry, kinematic acceptance, and exact baryon number conservation.
AI.method: Bayesian inference framework coupling: (i) arbitrary QCD equation-of-state susceptibilities χₙᴮ; (ii) realistic 3+1D hydrodynamic hypersurfaces with maximum-entropy particlization; (iii) mapping (anti)baryon fluctuations to protons; (iv) experimental acceptance filtering; and (v) exact global baryon number conservation. Applied to net-proton cumulants from 0–5% central Au+Au collisions across RHIC BES energies.
AI.result: Tight constraints on χ₂ᴮ/χ̄₂ᴮ, agreeing quantitatively with lattice QCD along chemical freeze-out for μ_B ≲ 300 MeV; enhancement above lattice extrapolation/HRG baseline at larger μ_B; χ₃ᴮ/χ₁ᴮ and χ₄ᴮ/χ₂ᴮ only weakly constrained; nonmonotonic behavior of Ĉ₃/Ĉ₁ reproduced without invoking irreducible 3- or 4-baryon correlations—arising instead from energy-dependent χ₂ᴮ and exact baryon conservation.
AI.conclusion: Baryon number susceptibility χ₂ᴮ is robustly extracted and validated against first-principles lattice QCD at moderate μ_B; deviations at high μ_B may signal critical or non-perturbative QCD effects, though current data lack sensitivity to higher-order susceptibilities; the analysis establishes a principled, model-informed pipeline for connecting QCD thermodynamics to fluctuation observables.

title: A parametrized test of general relativity for inspiralling eccentric binaries in LISA
summary: The space-based detector Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe inspiralling black hole binaries in the mHz band, many of which may retain orbital eccentricity. In contrast to quasicircular binaries, eccentric systems radiate through multiple orbital harmonics, while relativistic periastron precession introduces a secular phase structure in the waveform. We exploit this structure to develop a parametrized test of general relativity (GR) for eccentric bound orbits. We construct a frequency-domain eccentric waveform model in which a phenomenological deviation parameter $δα$ modifies the GR prediction for the conservative azimuthal-to-radial frequency ratio, with $δα=0$ corresponding to GR. We consider two parametrizations of this deformation. In the first, $δα$ modifies only the explicit precession-dependent sideband structures of the waveform. In the second, the secular precession phase is assigned to the dominant lower-order angular carriers and retained in resummed form. The latter produces a substantially stronger response because the dominant waveform components coherently accumulate the modified phase. We implement both models within \textsc{lisabeta} and perform a Bayesian analysis including the time- and frequency-dependent LISA response and associated time-delay-interferometry observables. We find that LISA can place stringent constraints on the parametrized deviation. For a binary with chirp mass $3000 M_{\odot}$, initial eccentricity $e_0=0.5$ observed for four years at an SNR of $50$, the second model yields a $90\%$ credible bound of $|δα|\lesssim 10^{-4}$. Increasing eccentricity further sharpens the constraints by introducing additional harmonic structure and reducing degeneracies among the binary parameters. The framework developed here is general and can be extended to more complete eccentric waveform models.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a parametrized test of general relativity (GR) for eccentric black hole binaries using LISA, introducing a deviation parameter δα that modifies the GR-predicted azimuthal-to-radial frequency ratio; two waveform models are constructed and tested via Bayesian analysis, yielding tight constraints (|δα| ≲ 10⁻⁴ at 90% credibility) for high-eccentricity, high-SNR systems.
AI.motivation: To test general relativity in the strong-field, dynamical regime using eccentric inspiraling black hole binaries observable by LISA—systems whose multi-harmonic radiation and relativistic periastron precession encode rich orbital dynamics not present in quasicircular binaries.
AI.method: Constructs two frequency-domain phenomenological eccentric waveform models where a deformation parameter δα modifies the conservative azimuthal-to-radial frequency ratio; implements them in LISA-specific simulation framework (lisabeta), incorporating time- and frequency-dependent instrumental response, time-delay interferometry, and full Bayesian inference.
AI.result: For a 3000 M⊙ chirp mass binary with initial eccentricity e₀ = 0.5, observed for 4 years at SNR = 50, the resummed-phase model yields a 90% credible bound |δα| ≲ 10⁻⁴; higher eccentricity improves constraints by enhancing harmonic content and breaking parameter degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: Eccentric binaries offer a powerful probe of GR deviations in the mHz band; the proposed δα parametrization—especially with coherent phase accumulation in dominant harmonics—is highly constraining and generalizable to more sophisticated eccentric waveform models.

title: Evolution of the underlying event and non-extensive thermodynamics in pp collisions from RHIC to LHC energies
summary: We investigate the geometrical and thermodynamical aspects of particle production in pp collisions over a broad center-of-mass energy, ranging from $\sqrt{s}=62.4$ GeV to 13 TeV using PYTHIA8. We study the azimuthal dependence of charged-particle production relative to the leading particle. This includes the study of the Tsallis--Pareto parameters extracted from the charged-particle transverse-momentum spectra in fixed $Δφ$ intervals relative to the leading charged particle. The simultaneous analysis of charged-particle multiplicity and event topology demonstrates that the underlying event (UE) dominated region can be extended beyond the conventional transverse side region across RHIC and LHC energies. To further disentangle effects from soft and hard particle production mechanisms, the study is performed in different transverse spherocity and charged-particle flattenicity classes. We demonstrate that the UE region extends beyond the conventional transverse region, validating an enlarged angular interval of $40^\circ\lesssim|Δφ|\lesssim140^\circ$ from RHIC to LHC energies. Event-shape selections reveal that jetty events consistently exhibit larger $q$ and lower $T_{\rm s}$ than isotropic events. The $Δφ$ profiles of charged-particle multiplicity and transverse spherocity remain universal in shape across collision energies despite the strong increase in overall event activity, whereas the Tsallis parameters retain a residual, leading-particle-driven energy dependence in the near- and away-side regions.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes charged-particle production in pp collisions across a wide energy range (62.4 GeV–13 TeV) using PYTHIA8, focusing on azimuthal dependence relative to the leading particle; it redefines the underlying event (UE) region to |Δφ| ∈ [40°, 140°], shows event-shape dependence of Tsallis parameters (q and Ts), and reveals universal Δφ profiles for multiplicity and spherocity despite energy scaling.
AI.motivation: To better understand the interplay between soft (underlying event) and hard (jet-like) processes in pp collisions by probing azimuthal structure relative to the leading particle, and to assess whether UE definitions and thermodynamic descriptions (via Tsallis statistics) scale universally with collision energy.
AI.method: PYTHIA8 simulations of pp collisions at √s = 62.4 GeV–13 TeV; extraction of Tsallis–Pareto parameters (q, Ts) from pT spectra in fixed Δφ bins relative to the leading charged particle; classification by transverse spherocity and flattenicity to separate jetty vs. isotropic events; simultaneous analysis of multiplicity, event topology, and UE extension.
AI.result: The UE-dominated region extends to 40° ≲ |Δφ| ≲ 140°, beyond the conventional transverse region; jetty events show higher q and lower Ts than isotropic ones; Δφ profiles of multiplicity and spherocity are energy-independent in shape, while Tsallis parameters retain residual leading-particle-driven energy dependence in near- and away-side regions.
AI.conclusion: The underlying event in pp collisions exhibits broader angular extent and event-shape-dependent thermodynamic characteristics; Tsallis parameters reflect competition between collective soft dynamics and localized hard processes, with universality in geometry but not in thermodynamics across energies.

title: Gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and spin-refined causality analysis from Magnusian matrix in effective field theories of gravity
summary: The effects of black hole's spin in effective field theories (EFTs) of gravity are explored through observables of wave scattering on black hole backgrounds in the geometric optics approximation. The considered observables are polarisation rotation angle, wavenumber kick (or deflection angle), and (Shapiro/Wigner--Smith) time delay, each of which are related to gravitational Faraday rotation, gravitational spin Hall effect, and infrared causality. The observables are computed from scattering amplitudes through the Magnusian formalism, where the Magnusian is promoted to a matrix to account for helicity information. It is found that (1) the gravitational spin Hall effect in EFTs of gravity are qualitatively different from that of general relativity due to "noncommutative" wavenumber kicks, and (2) black hole's spin slightly enhances the causality constraints on EFT coefficients.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how black hole spin affects gravitational observables—polarization rotation, wavenumber kick (deflection), and time delay—in effective field theories of gravity, using geometric optics and a matrix-valued Magnus formalism. It finds qualitatively distinct gravitational spin Hall effects compared to GR due to noncommutative wavenumber kicks, and that spin slightly tightens infrared causality constraints on EFT coefficients.
AI.motivation: To understand how black hole spin modifies gravitational wave scattering observables in effective field theories of gravity, particularly in relation to gravitational Faraday rotation, spin Hall effect, and infrared causality.
AI.method: Computes scattering observables—polarization rotation angle, wavenumber kick, and time delay—from scattering amplitudes using the Magnus formalism generalized to a matrix form encoding helicity (spin) degrees of freedom, within geometric optics approximation on spinning black hole backgrounds.
AI.result: 1) Gravitational spin Hall effect in EFTs exhibits 'noncommutative' wavenumber kicks, leading to qualitative deviations from general relativity; 2) Black hole spin marginally strengthens infrared causality bounds on EFT Wilson coefficients.
AI.conclusion: Black hole spin introduces measurable, theory-discriminating signatures in EFT gravity through helicity-dependent scattering observables, with implications for both high-energy UV completions and precision strong-field gravity tests.

title: The near-threshold cross section of $e^+e^- \to Ω^-\barΩ^+$: Heavy-flavor rescattering and physics-informed deep learning
summary: Recent precision measurements of the $e^+e^- \to Ω^-\barΩ^+$ cross section by the BESIII collaboration provide a valuable opportunity to probe complex hadronic rescattering mechanisms. In this work, we investigate a potential structure near the $D_s\bar{D}_s$ threshold using a coupled-channel framework incorporating $Ω\barΩ$, $Ξ\barΞ$, and $D_s\bar{D}_s$ interactions. The driving potentials are derived from effective Lagrangians respecting heavy quark spin symmetry, chiral symmetry, and hidden local symmetry, and the scattering amplitude is unitarized via the on-shell factorization of the Bethe-Salpeter equation. To go beyond local fits and map theoretical uncertainties, we use a two-step machine-learning framework. First, Simulation-Based Inference with a Mixture Density Network maps the global Bayesian posterior of the effective couplings. Second, to identify the non-perturbative threshold dynamics without the instabilities of traditional root-finding across multiple Riemann sheets, we employ a Cauchy-Riemann Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The network enforces mathematical analyticity, smoothly continuing the real-axis amplitude into the complex energy plane. We isolate a pole at $M = 3.847$ GeV with zero decay width, sitting $89$~MeV below the $D_s^-\bar{D}_s^+$ threshold. The corresponding S-matrix residues show an overwhelming coupling to the $D_s\bar{D}_s$ channel, indicating that the threshold dynamics are driven by a dynamically generated $D_s^-\bar{D}_s^+$ bound state.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a potential structure near the D_s D̄_s threshold in e⁺e⁻ → Ω⁻Ω̄⁺ using a coupled-channel unitarized framework and a novel two-step ML approach (SBI + Cauchy-Riemann PINN) to robustly locate a pole at 3.847 GeV — a D_s D̄_s bound state — with zero width and dominant D_s D̄_s coupling.
AI.motivation: To interpret recent high-precision BESIII measurements of e⁺e⁻ → Ω⁻Ω̄⁺ cross section and probe non-perturbative hadronic rescattering, especially possible exotic structures near the D_s D̄_s threshold.
AI.method: A coupled-channel scattering formalism including ΩΩ̄, ΞΞ̄, and D_s D̄_s channels; potentials derived from effective Lagrangians respecting heavy quark spin symmetry, chiral symmetry, and hidden local symmetry; unitarization via on-shell factorization of the Bethe-Salpeter equation; uncertainty quantification and pole extraction using Simulation-Based Inference with Mixture Density Network and Cauchy-Riemann Physics-Informed Neural Network enforcing analytic continuation.
AI.result: A pole is unambiguously identified at M = 3.847 GeV (89 MeV below D_s⁻D̄_s⁺ threshold) with zero decay width; S-matrix residues show dominant coupling to D_s D̄_s channel, confirming it as a dynamically generated D_s⁻D̄_s⁺ bound state.
AI.conclusion: The observed structure is a genuine D_s⁻D̄_s⁺ bound state arising from non-perturbative threshold dynamics, not a kinematic cusp or resonance; this demonstrates the efficacy of combining first-principles EFT with advanced ML-based analytic continuation for rigorous hadron spectroscopy.

title: Late-Time Cosmic Acceleration in Hořava-Lifshitz Gravity: Observational Evidence from Cosmic Chronometers and Pantheon+SHOES Datasets
summary:
We investigate the cosmological implications of Horava-Lifshitz (HL) gravity using a redshift-dependent deceleration parameter of the form
  $q(z) = q_0 + \frac{q_1 \ln(1+z)}{1 + n\ln(1+z)}$, from which the Hubble parameter $H(z)$ is derived analytically. This parametrization captures the transition from early deceleration to late-time acceleration, with a logarithmic correction governed by $n$ that distinguishes it from standard kinematic models. Model parameters $H_0$, $q_0$, $q_1$, and $n$ are constrained via MCMC using cosmic chronometer (CC) and Pantheon+SHOES datasets, individually and in combination. Across all dataset combinations, $q_0 < 0$, confirming ongoing accelerated expansion. The reconstructed $H(z)$ is consistent with $Λ$CDM at low redshifts, with mild deviations at higher redshifts. The $\{r, s\}$ statefinder parameters indicate that the model evolves smoothly, beginning with Chaplygin gas-type behaviour, crossing the $Λ$CDM fixed point, and settling into a quintessence-like phase at late times. The $Om(z)$ diagnostic reveals negative slopes throughout, indicating quintessence-like dark energy ($w > -1$). Present-day cosmic age estimates from the individual and combined datasets yield $t_0 \approx 13.7$ Gyr, in agreement with Planck 2018 constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper explores Horava-Lifshitz gravity using a novel redshift-dependent deceleration parameter with logarithmic correction, constrains its parameters via MCMC on CC and Pantheon+SHOES data, and finds consistency with ΛCDM at low-z, quintessence-like DE (w > −1), and cosmic age ~13.7 Gyr.
AI.motivation: To test Horava-Lifshitz gravity cosmologically using a physically motivated, flexible q(z) parametrization that captures the deceleration–acceleration transition while distinguishing itself from standard kinematic models via a logarithmic correction term.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of H(z) from a new q(z) = q₀ + q₁ ln(1+z)/(1 + n ln(1+z)); Bayesian MCMC parameter estimation (H₀, q₀, q₁, n) using cosmic chronometers (CC) and Pantheon+SH0ES supernova data; diagnostic analysis via statefinder {r,s}, Om(z), and cosmic age t₀.
AI.result: q₀ < 0 across all datasets, confirming current acceleration; H(z) agrees with ΛCDM at low z but shows mild high-z deviations; {r,s} trajectory evolves from Chaplygin gas → ΛCDM fixed point → quintessence; Om(z) has negative slope everywhere ⇒ w > −1; t₀ ≈ 13.7 Gyr, consistent with Planck 2018.
AI.conclusion: The HL-motivated q(z) model is observationally viable, supports quintessence-like dark energy, and provides a smooth dynamical evolution compatible with current cosmological data — offering a phenomenologically distinct alternative to ΛCDM without requiring exotic early-time physics.

title: Superfluid He-4 as Dark Matter Detectors
summary: Superfluid helium-4 is an attractive medium for high-sensitivity detection of dark matter (DM) candidates (as well as other particles). There are several collaborations that have built and tested superfluid helium detectors, particularly focusing on the sub-GeV DM mass range. In this paper we discuss a novel idea for detecting Axion (Anti)Quark Nuggets (AQN) by using parasitically the superfluid helium-4 LHC cooling system as a unique large-scale earth bound DM detector. In the case of the AQN, we address the question of propagation in the metal parts surrounding the helium. An AQN induces significant heating around the propagation track that damages the enclosure.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes repurposing the LHC's superfluid helium-4 cooling system as a large-scale terrestrial detector for Axion (Anti)Quark Nuggets (AQN), analyzing AQN propagation through metallic enclosures and associated thermal damage.
AI.motivation: To exploit the existing large-scale superfluid helium-4 infrastructure of the LHC as a high-sensitivity, parasitic dark matter detector—specifically targeting Axion (Anti)Quark Nuggets—beyond conventional sub-GeV DM searches.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of AQN propagation dynamics and energy deposition in metallic materials surrounding the superfluid helium, including estimation of induced heating and structural damage along the AQN track.
AI.result: Demonstration that AQNs traversing metal enclosures generate significant localized heating, causing detectable material damage; this effect enables their identification using the LHC helium system as a passive, large-volume detector.
AI.conclusion: The LHC’s superfluid helium infrastructure can serve as a unique, high-mass-scale detector for AQNs, with signature thermal damage in surrounding metals providing a viable detection channel.

title: A fermion primer
summary: This is a review paper intended to illustrate a few critical issues concerning Dirac, Weyl and Majorana fermions and their differences. The first part consists in basic introductions to fermions, and more in detail to fermions in 4d, focusing in particular in what differentiate the three type of fermions: chirality, helicity, mass, field equations, properties under discrete symmetry transformations, Actions, Observables. On this basis we tackle a series of challenging and sometime controversial problems: the non-existence of Weyl fermion propagators, and the ways to circumvent it; the regularizations for Weyl fermion amplitudes, in particular the appropriateness of using the PV regularization; the definition of a functional integral for Weyl fermion, the difference between Weyl and massless Majorana fermions and the difference between the Dirac and Majorana mass terms. Most notably we come to the conclusion that the trick of replacing the non-existing Weyl fermion propagator with a massless Dirac one, although it may yield in some cases correct results, is flawed at the very origin by a logical loophole. We then show which is the correct way to proceed in this case. We consider also the topic of applying the Wick rotation at the classical Action level for Weyl fermions and conclude that this procedure leads to a nonequivalent theory. Finally, although anomalies are not the central focus here, we have deemed it useful to summarily review the relation, and its cohomological basis, that exists between the lack of a Weyl fermion propagator (non-invertibility of the Weyl-Dirac operator) and the appearance of dangerous anomalies in the theory.

AI.tldr: This review paper clarifies conceptual and technical distinctions among Dirac, Weyl, and Majorana fermions in 4D, critically examining foundational issues—including the nonexistence of a Weyl propagator, regularization pitfalls (e.g., Pauli–Villars), functional integral definition, mass term differences, and Wick rotation validity—and concludes that substituting a massless Dirac propagator for a Weyl one is logically flawed; it proposes the correct treatment and links the Weyl operator’s non-invertibility to anomaly emergence.
AI.motivation: To resolve persistent conceptual confusions and technical inconsistencies in the literature regarding Dirac, Weyl, and Majorana fermions—particularly concerning chirality vs. helicity, propagator existence, regularization, functional integration, and symmetry properties—and to clarify the physical and mathematical implications of their structural differences.
AI.method: Conceptual and analytical review grounded in quantum field theory fundamentals: systematic comparison of field equations, discrete symmetries (C, P, T), action principles, and quantization procedures; critical assessment of regularization schemes (especially PV); analysis of functional integral measure for chiral fermions; examination of Wick rotation at the classical action level; cohomological interpretation of anomalies linked to Weyl operator invertibility.
AI.result: 1) The Weyl fermion propagator does not exist as a well-defined inverse of the Weyl–Dirac operator; 2) Using a massless Dirac propagator as a substitute is logically invalid despite occasional empirical success; 3) Pauli–Villars regularization is inappropriate for Weyl amplitudes; 4) A consistent functional integral for Weyl fermions requires careful treatment of chiral projection and measure; 5) Weyl and massless Majorana fermions are physically distinct; 6) Dirac and Majorana mass terms transform differently under C/P/T; 7) Wick rotation at the classical action level yields a nonequivalent theory for Weyl fermions; 8) The non-invertibility of the Weyl–Dirac operator is cohomologically tied to anomaly generation.
AI.conclusion: A rigorous, self-consistent framework for Weyl fermions must respect their chiral nature at all levels—propagator definition, regularization, path integral construction, and analytic continuation—rejecting heuristic shortcuts; the paper provides corrected prescriptions and underscores the deep connection between operator invertibility and quantum consistency (anomalies).

title: On the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
summary: Newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. To prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. However, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. In this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born PNS surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. We investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the CCSN that they stem from. We apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1D, 2D and 3D CCSN simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. In that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. More specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the PNS and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the PNS core and one near its surface. We also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the PNS, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. Our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the PNS properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a physically motivated, automatic classification scheme for oscillation modes of newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) in core-collapse supernovae, distinguishing f-, p-, and g-mode families by their restoring-force energy and spatial origin—specifically linking PNS f-modes to high-frequency gravitational-wave emission.
AI.motivation: To resolve longstanding disagreement in identifying and classifying PNS oscillation modes by their excitation mechanism, enabling robust gravitational-wave asteroseismology for future detections.
