AI.method: A novel classification scheme based on the energy of restoring forces and spatial origin of modes; applied to 28 non-rotating 1D/2D/3D CCSN simulations across two codes, multiple progenitors, and equations of state.
AI.result: Identification of two f- and p-mode families (PNS vs. shock) and two g-mode families (PNS core vs. near-surface convectively stable regions); PNS f-mode dominates high-frequency GW emission due to surface density gradient.
AI.conclusion: The automatic, physically grounded classification is consistent across models and enables systematic, observation-ready parameter estimation of PNS properties from gravitational-wave mode frequencies.

title: TauPolaris: reconstructing tau lepton polarimetric vectors with conditional normalizing flows
summary: The kinematics of tau lepton decay products depend on the tau spin, giving access to the spin correlations and CP structure of the process that produced them. The optimal spin observable is the polarimetric vector, which points along the most likely direction of the tau spin. Determining it requires the momenta of the neutrinos produced in the tau decays, which escape detection and must therefore be inferred. We present TauPolaris, a tool for reconstructing tau polarimetric vectors by estimating the undetected neutrino momenta with a conditional normalizing flow. Rather than performing a point regression, the method models the full conditional density of the neutrino kinematics, providing both the most likely configuration for each event and an estimate of its uncertainty. The resolution of the reconstructed spin observables improves on that obtained from networks trained with a mean-squared-error loss. Using simulated LHC proton-proton collisions, including detector resolution effects, we demonstrate the method in three applications. For tau leptons produced in Higgs boson decays, we show that the presence of quantum entanglement can be distinguished from its absence with a significance of at least $4.3σ$ at the High-Luminosity LHC. We demonstrate an 18% improvement in the sensitivity to CP violation in $H\rightarrowττ$ decays. Finally, we introduce new variables for suppressing the $Z\rightarrowττ$ background in Higgs boson searches.

AI.tldr: TauPolaris uses a conditional normalizing flow to reconstruct tau polarimetric vectors by modeling the full conditional density of undetected neutrino momenta, improving spin observable resolution and enabling enhanced CP violation sensitivity, entanglement detection, and background suppression in H→ττ analyses.
AI.motivation: Tau lepton decay kinematics encode spin information relevant for probing spin correlations and CP structure; however, missing neutrinos hinder precise reconstruction of the polarimetric vector—the optimal spin observable.
AI.method: TauPolaris employs a conditional normalizing flow to model the full conditional probability density of neutrino momenta given observed decay products, enabling both maximum-likelihood estimation and uncertainty quantification—superior to point-wise regression with MSE loss.
AI.result: Improved resolution of reconstructed polarimetric vectors; 4.3σ discrimination between entangled vs. non-entangled H→ττ events at HL-LHC; 18% gain in CP violation sensitivity; novel observables for Z→ττ background suppression in Higgs searches.
AI.conclusion: Conditional normalizing flows provide a statistically principled, uncertainty-aware framework for neutrino momentum inference, significantly advancing tau spin physics capabilities at the LHC.

title: Event-by-event analysis of chiral charge separation in $p^{\uparrow}+$Au collisions within an improved AMPT model
summary: We study the charge separation induced by chiral magnetic effect (CME) in $p^{\uparrow}$+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV event-by-event with an improved string-melting AMPT model. In this model, an impact-parameter-dependent formation-time delay is introduced to reduce the peak Bjorken energy density from $\sim$2 to $\sim$0.3 GeV/fm$^3$ and reproduces the illiptic flow $v_2(p_T)$ measured by PHENIX in $p+$Au simultaneously. The event-by-event CME source, whose quark momentum-exchange fraction scales with $|\mathbf{B}|_{\mathrm{event}}/|\mathbf{B}|_{\mathrm{max}}$ and is capped at the 7\% value from Au+Au, transmits the field geometry directly to the observable. We find that the initial correlator shows a clear scheme hierarchy tracking $B^2$. The parton cascade preserves $\sim$80--90\% of the signal, while coalescence and ART hadronic rescattering dissipate the bulk, leaving $\sim$10--30\% in the final state. The $γ_{OS}/γ_{SS}$ splitting remains visible. These results support the use of the inter-scheme difference $Δγ_{\mathrm{IV}}-Δγ_{\mathrm{II}}$ as an essentially background-free CME observable as we proposed in previous work.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates chiral magnetic effect (CME)-induced charge separation in polarized proton–gold collisions using an improved string-melting AMPT model with impact-parameter-dependent formation-time delay; it quantifies CME signal survival through partonic and hadronic stages and validates Δγ_IV − Δγ_II as a background-suppressed CME observable.
AI.motivation: To isolate and quantify the chiral magnetic effect (CME) signal in small-system collisions (p↑+Au), where backgrounds dominate and conventional observables suffer from contamination, requiring a controlled, geometry-sensitive CME source and realistic dynamical modeling.
AI.method: Event-by-event simulations in an improved string-melting AMPT framework: (i) introduced impact-parameter-dependent formation-time delay to lower peak energy density and simultaneously reproduce PHENIX v₂(pₜ); (ii) constructed event-specific CME source proportional to |B|_event/|B|_max, capped at 7% based on Au+Au data; (iii) tracked signal evolution across parton cascade, coalescence, and ART hadronic rescattering; (iv) analyzed γ_OS/γ_SS splitting and inter-scheme differences Δγ_IV − Δγ_II.
AI.result: Initial CME correlator exhibits clear B² hierarchy; parton cascade preserves 80–90% of signal; coalescence and hadronic rescattering suppress signal to 10–30% in final state; γ_OS/γ_SS splitting remains observable; Δγ_IV − Δγ_II is confirmed as robust, essentially background-free CME observable.
AI.conclusion: The study provides quantitative evidence that a geometry-encoded, event-by-event CME signal survives final-state interactions sufficiently to be isolated via Δγ_IV − Δγ_II, supporting its use for CME search in small systems like p↑+Au.

title: Probing scalarized wormholes through quasi-periodic oscillations and spinning particle dynamics
summary: We investigate the dynamics of test particles in a three-parameter scalarized wormhole spacetime within Einstein-scalar field theory. For spinless particles, we derive the orbital and epicyclic frequencies and compute twin-peak QPO spectra using the ER3 and ER4 resonance models. The scalar coupling parameter $g_s$ shifts the innermost stable circular orbit to larger radii and systematically modifies the characteristic 3:2 resonance condition. Extending to spinning particles via the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism, we find that spin-curvature coupling significantly alters the effective potential and innermost stable circular orbit parameters. The maximum physically admissible spin increases monotonically with the scalar coupling. Analysis of particle collisions near the wormhole throat reveals that both scalar coupling and relative spin orientation determine collision energetics, with anti-aligned spin configurations producing substantially higher energies. Our results suggest that the combined effects of scalar coupling and spin-curvature interaction leave distinct imprints on QPO frequencies and collision processes, potentially providing observable signatures for distinguishing scalarized wormholes from standard black holes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies test particle dynamics in a three-parameter scalarized wormhole spacetime, analyzing orbital/epicyclic frequencies, QPO spectra (via ER3/ER4 models), and spin effects using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism; it finds that scalar coupling $g_s$ and spin-curvature interaction shift ISCO, modify resonance conditions, enhance collision energies (especially for anti-aligned spins), and yield potentially observable signatures distinguishing scalarized wormholes from black holes.
AI.motivation: To identify observable signatures—particularly in QPOs and high-energy collisions—that can distinguish scalarized wormholes from standard black holes in Einstein-scalar field theory.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of orbital and epicyclic frequencies for spinless particles; computation of twin-peak QPO spectra using ER3 and ER4 resonance models; extension to spinning particles via the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations; analysis of effective potential, ISCO, and center-of-mass energy for particle collisions near the wormhole throat.
AI.result: Scalar coupling $g_s$ shifts ISCO outward and modifies the 3:2 resonance condition; spin-curvature coupling alters effective potential and ISCO parameters; maximum admissible spin increases monotonically with $g_s$; anti-aligned spin configurations yield significantly higher center-of-mass collision energies near the throat.
AI.conclusion: The joint influence of scalar coupling and spin-curvature interaction produces distinctive imprints on QPO frequencies and particle collision energetics—offering promising observational diagnostics for scalarized wormholes versus black holes.

title: Hilbert Series of Pseudoscalar Mesons: Operators and Sum Rules
summary: We construct the complete non-redundant basis of operators built from pseudoscalar mesons using the Hilbert series method, subject to the global flavor symmetry $SU(3)_L \times SU(3)_R \times SU(2)_{L_H} \times SU(2)_{R_H}$, together with the underlying shift symmetry. The SM weak interactions are incorporated systematically by promoting the CKM matrix elements to spurion fields transforming under the global symmetry. The resulting operator basis provides a model-independent parametrization of two- and three-body weak decay amplitudes of heavy mesons, with the corresponding Wilson coefficients serving as reduced hadronic amplitudes. We demonstrate that all amplitude sum rules follow directly from the structure of the operator basis and propose an unfolding procedure that connects the effective operators to their possible ultraviolet origins. Our framework reproduces the known flavor relations while predicting additional identities arising from the symmetry-constrained operator basis.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a complete, non-redundant effective operator basis for pseudoscalar mesons using the Hilbert series method under a specific flavor symmetry and shift symmetry; incorporates SM weak interactions via CKM spurions; provides a model-independent parametrization of heavy-meson weak decays; derives amplitude sum rules from basis structure; and proposes an unfolding procedure linking operators to UV origins.
AI.motivation: To establish a systematic, symmetry-based, model-independent framework for parametrizing weak decay amplitudes of heavy pseudoscalar mesons, capturing all possible hadronic effects via Wilson coefficients while respecting underlying chiral and flavor symmetries.
AI.method: Hilbert series technique to enumerate independent operators built from pseudoscalar mesons, subject to SU(3)_L × SU(3)_R × SU(2)_{L_H} × SU(2)_{R_H} global symmetry and shift symmetry; CKM matrix elements promoted to spurion fields to systematically incorporate electroweak interactions; use of group-theoretic constraints to eliminate redundancy and derive amplitude relations.
AI.result: A complete, non-redundant effective operator basis for two- and three-body weak decays of heavy mesons; derivation of all known and new amplitude sum rules directly from basis structure; identification of Wilson coefficients as reduced hadronic amplitudes; proposal of an unfolding procedure connecting low-energy operators to potential UV completions.
AI.conclusion: The symmetry-constrained operator basis fully encodes model-independent hadronic physics in heavy-meson weak decays; amplitude relations are structural consequences—not dynamical assumptions—and the framework both reproduces established flavor relations and predicts novel identities testable in experiment.

title: Distance-Higuchi Bounds on Inflationary Field Ranges and Lifetimes
summary: We show that quasi-de Sitter inflation driven by a nearly flat scalar potential has a finite polynomial lifespan dictated by the interplay between the swampland Distance Conjecture and the generalized Higuchi bound. By analyzing classical scalar rolling and quantum stochastic diffusion, we demonstrate that for any arbitrarily high but fixed statistical confidence, a universe cannot live longer than $\sim \min\left\{\ln(\frac{1}{H})\frac{\sqrt V}{V'},V^{-\frac{d-1}{2}}\ln^2(\frac{1}{H})\right\}$ in reduced Planck units while remaining Higuchi-consistent, where $H$ is the Hubble parameter, $V$ is the scalar potential, $d$ is the number of spacetime dimensions, and prime denotes derivative with respect to the scalar field. This bound despite being weaker than the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture, which has been argued for classical cosmologies that flow to the asymptotic of the field space without tunneling, is powerful given its minimal quantum gravity input and applicability to all points in the moduli space.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a finite lifespan bound for quasi-de Sitter inflation, derived from the swampland Distance Conjecture and generalized Higuchi bound, incorporating both classical rolling and quantum stochastic effects.
AI.motivation: To reconcile long-lived quasi-de Sitter inflation with quantum gravity constraints, particularly the swampland conjectures and unitarity bounds in de Sitter space.
AI.method: Combined analysis of classical scalar field evolution and quantum stochastic diffusion in quasi-de Sitter spacetime; derivation of lifespan bound using the swampland Distance Conjecture and generalized Higuchi bound.
AI.result: A finite polynomial inflationary lifespan bound: ~ min{ ln(1/H) √V / V′ , V^{−(d−1)/2} ln²(1/H) } (in reduced Planck units), valid for any fixed statistical confidence and applicable across the moduli space.
AI.conclusion: Quasi-de Sitter inflation cannot be eternal—even with arbitrarily flat potentials—due to unavoidable quantum-gravitational and unitarity constraints; the derived bound is weaker than TCC but more generally applicable with minimal quantum gravity input.

title: Nucleon electromagnetic form factors in nonlocal chiral effective theory
summary: In this paper, we calculate the pion one-loop corrections to the electromagnetic form factors of the nucleon up to $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ order in the nonlocal framework. To systematically investigate the role of vector-meson dominance in the model, we also include the leading-order nucleon-vector-meson coupling. Owing to the renormalization-scheme dependence of chiral low-energy coupling constants (LECs), we refit these constants to the nucleon magnetic moments, electromagnetic radii, and the $Q^2$-dependence of the electromagnetic form factors. Compared with the previous local analysis, the model results show that, in the nonlocal framework, the $Q^2$-dependence of the electromagnetic form factors in the large-$Q^2$ region is significantly improved and are consistent with experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper computes pion one-loop corrections to nucleon electromagnetic form factors up to O(p⁴) in a nonlocal chiral effective field theory, incorporates vector-meson dominance via leading nucleon–vector-meson couplings, and refits low-energy constants using nucleon magnetic moments, radii, and Q²-dependence of form factors—yielding improved agreement with data at large Q² compared to local approaches.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess the role of vector-meson dominance and improve the description of the Q²-dependence of nucleon electromagnetic form factors—particularly at large Q²—where local chiral EFT fails.
AI.method: Nonlocal chiral effective field theory at O(p⁴); includes pion one-loop contributions and leading-order nucleon–vector-meson couplings; renormalization-scheme-independent refitting of low-energy coupling constants to experimental observables (magnetic moments, charge/magnetic radii, and Q²-dependence of G_E and G_M).
AI.result: The nonlocal framework significantly improves the large-Q² behavior of the electromagnetic form factors (G_E and G_M), achieving better consistency with experimental data than previous local calculations.
AI.conclusion: Nonlocality and explicit vector-meson degrees of freedom are essential for quantitatively describing the high-momentum-transfer regime of nucleon electromagnetic structure within chiral EFT.

title: Quantum-Corrected Entropy Bounds on Black Hole Merger Efficiency
summary: We examine the entropy balance of black hole mergers in the presence of quantum gravity corrections described by the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP). Focusing on the coalescence of two non-spinning Schwarzschild black holes with unequal masses, we analyze the thermodynamic evolution from the initial binary system to the final merger remnant, explicitly accounting for energy loss through gravitational-wave emission. Using a logarithmically corrected entropy motivated by a quadratic GUP, we derive a generalized entropy change as a function of the gravitational-wave efficiency and the mass ratio of the merging components. The classical area theorem is recovered in the appropriate limit, while the GUP correction introduces a quantum-modified entropy bound that constrains the maximum allowed gravitational-wave energy emission. This bound is most restrictive for nearly equal-mass mergers, indicating an enhanced sensitivity of symmetric systems to quantum gravity effects.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how quantum gravity corrections, modeled via the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP), affect entropy balance during black hole mergers—specifically unequal-mass, non-spinning Schwarzschild black holes—revealing a quantum-modified entropy bound that limits gravitational-wave energy emission, especially in equal-mass cases.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum gravity effects, encoded in the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP), modify the thermodynamic consistency of black hole mergers—particularly whether entropy remains non-decreasing when quantum corrections to black hole entropy are included.
AI.method: The authors employ a logarithmically corrected black hole entropy formula derived from a quadratic GUP, model the merger of two non-spinning Schwarzschild black holes with arbitrary mass ratio, explicitly incorporate gravitational-wave energy loss, and compute the total entropy change across the process while enforcing energy conservation and horizon area constraints.
AI.result: A generalized entropy change expression is derived as a function of gravitational-wave efficiency and mass ratio; the classical area theorem (i.e., entropy non-decrease) is recovered in the semiclassical limit; a new quantum-modified entropy bound emerges, imposing an upper limit on radiated energy that is tightest for symmetric (equal-mass) mergers.
AI.conclusion: Quantum gravity corrections introduce a physically meaningful constraint on gravitational-wave emission in black hole mergers, enhancing sensitivity to quantum effects in symmetric configurations—suggesting that near-equal-mass mergers may serve as privileged probes of quantum gravity via entropy-balance considerations.

title: Moment of Inertia of an Interacting Bose Gas
summary: The response of many-body quantum systems to rotation can be characterized by the moment of inertia. For a classical gas, the moment of inertia can be expressed as the integral of the enthalpy density multiplied by the squared radial distance from the rotation axis. In quantum field theory, the finite rotation in the grand canonical ensemble demands the causality bound. This constraint imposes technical challenges in treating transverse momenta discretized with the Bessel function zeros. However, we define the moment of inertia in the limit of zero angular velocity, in which the causality constraint is irrelevant and ordinary quantum field theoretical techniques can be applied. We evaluate the moment of inertia in the $φ^4$ theory and find that, surprisingly, the interacting effects including the ring-diagram resummation are consistent with the classical expectation and the moment of inertia density remains proportional to the enthalpy density.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the moment of inertia for a rotating quantum many-body system in φ⁴ theory at zero angular velocity, showing that—despite quantum and interaction effects—the moment of inertia density remains proportional to the enthalpy density, matching classical expectations.
AI.motivation: To reconcile quantum field-theoretic treatment of rotating systems with classical mechanical intuition, particularly addressing technical difficulties from causality constraints at finite angular velocity.
AI.method: Defines moment of inertia in the zero-angular-velocity limit to bypass causality-bound complications; employs standard quantum field theory techniques, including ring-diagram resummation, in the grand canonical ensemble for φ⁴ theory.
AI.result: The moment of inertia density is found to be proportional to the enthalpy density, consistent with the classical expression ∫(enthalpy density) × r² dV, even with quantum corrections and interactions.
AI.conclusion: Quantum many-body corrections—including resummed ring diagrams—do not alter the proportionality between moment of inertia density and enthalpy density, affirming robustness of the classical relation in the zero-rotation limit.

title: Probing vorticity and fluctuations in a rotating hadron resonance gas at LHC energy
summary: A large vorticity produced in non-central ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions induces an effective chemical potential in both partonic and hadronic matter, thereby influencing the quark-hadron transition and its associated properties. In this work, we investigate the influence of rotation on hadron yields within the framework of Hadron Resonance Gas (HRG) model. Our results show that vorticity significantly modifies hadron yields and their ratios. Most notably, rotation enhances the $p/π^+$ ratio while suppressing the $K^+/π^+$ ratio, suggesting that these observables may serve as sensitive probes of the rotational properties of the medium created in heavy-ion collisions. To quantify the effect of rotation, the calculated dependence of the $p/π^+$ ratio on vorticity is compared with the centrality dependence of the $p/π$ ratio measured by the ALICE collaboration in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}$ = 5.02 TeV. From this comparison, we estimate the maximum vorticity produced at freeze-out for different collision centralities. In case of peripheral collisions, the freeze-out vorticity ($ω$) is found to reach an upper bound value of approximately 0.088 GeV, whereas for central collisions it is about 0.028 GeV. Furthermore, we investigate the effect of rotation on fluctuations of conserved quantities and their correlations. This study provides a quantitative framework for assessing the role of rotation in the thermodynamics of hadronic matter and its phenomenological consequences for heavy-ion collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how vorticity-induced effective chemical potentials affect hadron yields and fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions within the Hadron Resonance Gas model, finding that p/π⁺ and K⁺/π⁺ ratios are sensitive probes of freeze-out vorticity, with estimated ω ≈ 0.088 GeV (peripheral) and 0.028 GeV (central) Pb+Pb collisions at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV.
AI.motivation: To quantify how large vorticity generated in non-central ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions influences quark-hadron transition thermodynamics via rotation-induced effective chemical potentials in both partonic and hadronic phases.
AI.method: Extended Hadron Resonance Gas (HRG) model incorporating vorticity-dependent effective chemical potentials; analysis of hadron yield ratios (p/π⁺, K⁺/π⁺), centrality-dependent comparison with ALICE data, and study of conserved-charge fluctuations and correlations.
AI.result: Vorticity significantly enhances p/π⁺ ratio and suppresses K⁺/π⁺ ratio; freeze-out vorticity is estimated as ω ≈ 0.088 GeV (0–10% centrality) and ω ≈ 0.028 GeV (70–80% centrality); rotation also modifies fluctuations and correlations of conserved charges (e.g., baryon number, strangeness, charge).
AI.conclusion: Rotation is a key thermodynamic variable in HRG description of hadronic matter; p/π⁺ and K⁺/π⁺ ratios serve as quantitative probes of local vorticity at freeze-out; the framework enables systematic assessment of rotational effects on hadronization and observables in heavy-ion collisions.

title: The generalized second law as a thermodynamic selection criterion for dynamical dark energy
summary: The growing number of generalized horizon entropy proposals has led to a wide variety of modified cosmological models, yet there is currently no general physical principle capable of discriminating among them. We show that the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics provides such a criterion. Considering a general modified Friedmann framework described by an arbitrary function $f(H)$ of the Hubble parameter, and allowing the apparent horizon and the cosmic fluid to evolve out of thermal equilibrium, we derive model-independent constraints on the asymptotic scaling of the horizon entropy, $S_A\propto A^k$. We find that phantom evolution requires $k\ge(3ω-1)/(2ω)$, with $ω$ the total fluid equation of state, whereas quintessence imposes the complementary upper bound. Additionally, in the exact thermal equilibrium limit, the dynamical coupling strictly enforces $k \le 2$, recovering the non-equilibrium quintessence bound. The two bounds converge to the unique value $k=2$ as the phantom divide is approached, indicating that a smooth crossing of the phantom divide is thermodynamically associated with a quadratic entropy-area scaling, where the effective theory degenerates into a logarithmic gravity framework. Applying this criterion to representative generalized entropy models shows that many commonly used proposals are constrained by the generalized second law, whereas multiparameter constructions are naturally compatible with the required asymptotic behavior. Finally, we demonstrate that the same thermodynamic selection principle extends to derivative-dependent cosmologies described by $f(H,\dot H)$, highlighting its robustness beyond entropy functionals that depend only on the horizon area.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics to constrain horizon entropy scaling $S_A \propto A^k$ in modified Friedmann cosmologies, deriving model-independent bounds: phantom evolution requires $k \ge (3\omega-1)/(2\omega)$, quintessence imposes $k \le 2$, and smooth phantom-divide crossing forces $k = 2$, linking it to logarithmic gravity; the criterion applies broadly, including to $f(H,\dot H)$ cosmologies.
AI.motivation: To establish a physically grounded, model-independent criterion—via the generalized second law (GSL)—for discriminating among competing generalized horizon entropy proposals in modified cosmology, given the current lack of unifying physical principles.
AI.method: Derives asymptotic constraints on horizon entropy scaling $S_A \propto A^k$ within a general $f(H)$ Friedmann framework, incorporating out-of-equilibrium thermodynamics at the apparent horizon; analyzes phantom/quintessence regimes, exact equilibrium limit, and extends to $f(H,\dot H)$ models.
AI.result: Phantom evolution enforces $k \ge (3\omega-1)/(2\omega)$; quintessence yields $k \le 2$; equilibrium limit recovers $k \le 2$ strictly; phantom-divide crossing uniquely fixes $k = 2$, corresponding to logarithmic gravity; many single-parameter entropy models violate GSL bounds, while multiparameter ones satisfy them; bounds robustly extend to derivative-dependent $f(H,\dot H)$ cosmologies.
AI.conclusion: The generalized second law serves as a powerful, universal thermodynamic selection principle for horizon entropy in cosmology—excluding inconsistent entropy-area scalings, singling out $k=2$ at the phantom divide, and validating multiparameter entropy constructions and broader $f(H,\dot H)$ frameworks.

title: Two-Fluid Schwarzschild Solution
summary: We consider the interior two-fluid Schwarzschild solution. That is a model of compact (neutron) stars with admixed dark matter. The two constant energy densities generalize the interior Schwarschild solution to the case of two fluids (representing standard model matter and dark matter, for instance), interacting mutually solely by the common gravitational field. In general, the two-fluid core is surrounded by a one-fluid corona (envelope). Only for special parameters (the model depends on energy densities $e_1,e_2$ and central pressures $p_{\mathrm{c}1},p_{\mathrm{c}2}$ of the fluids), both fluids occupy the same region. Despite the sum of two energy densities in that region, the compactness bound of 8/9 is not exceeded. A conceivable object is one with a stark leakage of one fluid (e.g. dark matter) beyond the two-fluid core.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the interior Schwarzschild solution to a two-fluid model representing neutron stars with admixed dark matter, analyzing configurations where fluids coexist or segregate, and confirms that compactness remains below the 8/9 limit even with combined energy densities.
AI.motivation: To model compact stars (e.g., neutron stars) containing both standard matter and dark matter as two gravitationally coupled, non-interacting fluids—addressing astrophysical implications of dark matter admixture in stellar interiors.
AI.method: Analytical construction of the interior two-fluid Schwarzschild solution using Einstein’s equations for spherical symmetry, assuming constant energy densities $e_1$, $e_2$ and central pressures $p_{c1}$, $p_{c2}$ for each fluid; classification of core–corona and fully overlapping configurations based on parameter constraints.
AI.result: The two-fluid system admits both coexisting (same-region) and segregated (core–corona) configurations; compactness $M/R$ remains bounded by $8/9$, even when total energy density is sum of both fluids; leakage of one fluid (e.g., dark matter) beyond the core is physically viable.
AI.conclusion: The two-fluid Schwarzschild model provides a consistent relativistic framework for dark-matter-admixed compact stars without violating Buchdahl’s compactness bound, enabling exploration of observational signatures of dark matter distribution in stellar interiors.

title: Scaling of soft QGP signatures in relativistic lead, xenon and oxygen collisions in EPOS4
summary: The collective expansion and hydrodynamic evolution in heavy-ion collisions is well-established. However, whether femtometer-scale droplets of QGP are produced in small systems at high energies remains a fundamental open question. Analysis of Pb$-$Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.02 TeV, Xe$-$Xe at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.44 TeV and O$-$O collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$ = 5.36 TeV using EPOS4 is reported to make predictions and postdictions. The results are compared with ALICE data for Pb$-$Pb and Xe$-$Xe collisions. Charged particle multiplicity (d$N_{\mathrm{ch}}$/d$η$), transverse-momentum ($p_{\mathrm{T}}$) spectra for pions ($π^{\pm}$), kaons ($K^{\pm}$), and protons ($\text{p}(\overline{\text{p}})$) are studied. The inclusion of hadronic afterburner, UrQMD (Ultra-relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics) is found to be necessary to correctly describe baryon yields. $p_{\mathrm{T}}$-fluctuations are also studied via normalized $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ correlator, $\sqrt{\langle \langle Δp_{\mathrm{T},i}Δp_{\mathrm{T},j} \rangle \rangle}\mathrm{/} \langle \langle p_{\mathrm{T}} \rangle \rangle$. Lastly, anisotropic flow harmonics ($v_{\mathrm{2}} \{2\}$, $v_{\mathrm{3}} \{2\}$) are computed as a function of $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ and centrality. Since EPOS4 has not been extensively studied for flow observables, this study thereby provides a non-trivial assessment of its collective dynamics. The results are compared with experiment wherever data is available. Taken together, this study provides a unified description of soft observables from Pb$-$Pb through Xe$-$Xe down to O$-$O and offer quantitative guidance on how such collisions may inform of the properties of the QGP.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the EPOS4 model to simulate and compare soft observables—charged-particle multiplicity, $p_T$ spectra, $p_T$ fluctuations, and anisotropic flow harmonics—across Pb–Pb, Xe–Xe, and O–O collisions at LHC energies, assessing whether small-system collisions exhibit QGP-like collective behavior; inclusion of UrQMD afterburner is essential for baryon reproduction, and results provide a unified benchmark for QGP formation thresholds.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether femtometer-scale quark-gluon plasma (QGP) droplets are formed in small collision systems (e.g., O–O), by testing collective dynamics across system sizes using EPOS4—a hybrid hydro+transport model—and confronting predictions with ALICE data.
AI.method: EPOS4 simulations of Pb–Pb (√s_NN = 5.02 TeV), Xe–Xe (√s_NN = 5.44 TeV), and O–O (√s_NN = 5.36 TeV) collisions, including hadronic afterburner UrQMD; analysis of dN_ch/dη, identified particle p_T spectra (π±, K±, p/p̄), normalized p_T correlator ⟨⟨Δp_T,i Δp_T,j⟩⟩/⟨⟨p_T⟩⟩, and anisotropic flow v_2{2}, v_3{2} vs. p_T and centrality.
AI.result: UrQMD afterburner is crucial for reproducing baryon yields; EPOS4 qualitatively describes multiplicity, p_T spectra, and flow harmonics across all systems; v_2{2} and v_3{2} show system-size-dependent trends consistent with collective expansion; p_T fluctuations exhibit non-trivial centrality and system-size dependence; O–O results provide first quantitative EPOS4 predictions for smallest LHC system.
AI.conclusion: EPOS4 successfully provides a unified description of soft observables from large (Pb–Pb) to small (O–O) systems, supporting the interpretation that collective phenomena persist down to oxygen collisions—suggesting possible QGP formation even in sub-femtometer droplets, though definitive attribution requires further discrimination from non-hydrodynamic mechanisms.

title: Octupolar Gravitational Radiation in de Sitter Spacetime
summary: We derive the gravitational radiation generated by a localised matter source in de Sitter spacetime at octupolar order in the multipolar expansion, working in generalised harmonic gauge in the future Poincaré patch. The scalar, vector, and tensor perturbation equations are solved explicitly, taking into account the cosmological tail. This constitutes the first extension of the de Sitter multipolar expansion beyond quadrupolar order. A key technical ingredient is a universal multipole moment differentiation identity, which unifies the relations between multipole moments into a single recursive formula and enables a controlled extension to higher multipoles. Using the symmetric trace-free tensor formalism of Blanchet, Damour, and Iyer, we further develop a systematic translation of the radiative solution into a spherical harmonic basis, and apply it to both the quadrupolar and octupolar metric perturbations. This representation renders the angular structure of the radiation manifest, simplifies the verification of the linearised field equations, and facilitates direct comparison with Bondi-gauge and other perturbative treatments of de Sitter spacetime. Our results constitute a step toward a systematic ``multipolar post-de Sitter formalism''.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the multipolar expansion of gravitational radiation in de Sitter spacetime to octupolar order—beyond the standard quadrupole—for the first time, using generalized harmonic gauge and incorporating cosmological tail effects; it introduces a universal multipole differentiation identity and translates results into spherical harmonics for clarity and cross-gauge comparison.
AI.motivation: To extend gravitational-wave multipole formalism beyond quadrupole order in de Sitter spacetime, enabling higher-accuracy modeling of radiation in cosmological contexts and bridging gaps between harmonic-gauge, Bondi-gauge, and post-de Sitter approximations.
AI.method: Solves scalar, vector, and tensor linearised Einstein equations in generalized harmonic gauge within the future Poincaré patch of de Sitter spacetime; employs symmetric trace-free (STF) tensor formalism (Blanchet–Damour–Iyer); derives and applies a universal multipole moment differentiation identity; constructs radiative metric perturbations up to octupolar order and projects them onto spherical harmonics.
AI.result: Explicit octupolar-order gravitational radiation solution in de Sitter spacetime including cosmological tail contributions; derivation of a recursive, universal STF multipole differentiation identity; complete spherical harmonic decomposition of quadrupolar and octupolar metric perturbations; verification of linearised field equations and compatibility with Bondi-gauge structure.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes the first octupolar extension of the de Sitter multipolar formalism, provides technical tools (e.g., the universal differentiation identity) for systematic higher-order expansions, and lays groundwork for a multipolar post-de Sitter approximation scheme applicable to cosmological gravitational-wave sources.

title: Baryogenesis and CMB spectral distortion from Axions
summary: We discuss a mechanism for generating the baryon asymmetry in the early universe. We show that an axion-like particle can modify the related gauge field configurations in the Standard Model, thereby altering their dispersion relations. This change in the Chern-Simons number can source a violation of baryon number. We derive the relationship between the resulting baryon number and the evolution of the axion background. We estimate the baryon asymmetry produced via this mechanism and show that the observed value can be naturally achieved. We also show that axion photon coupling produces Cosmic Microwave Background spectral distortion. Our results show that the resulting distortion approaches a constant at low frequencies, unlike the conventional y-type and $μ$-type distortions.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel baryogenesis mechanism mediated by an axion-like particle (ALP) that modifies SM gauge field configurations, inducing Chern-Simons number evolution and thus B-violation; it quantitatively links baryon asymmetry to ALP dynamics and predicts a distinctive low-frequency constant CMB spectral distortion from ALP–photon coupling.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe via a new dynamical mechanism involving axion-like particles beyond conventional electroweak or GUT-scale baryogenesis.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of modified gauge field dispersion relations due to ALP coupling; computation of Chern-Simons number evolution and associated baryon number violation using semiclassical transport equations; estimation of baryon asymmetry yield from ALP background evolution; calculation of CMB spectral distortion induced by ALP–photon interaction in the thermal plasma.
AI.result: A quantitative relation between baryon number density and ALP field evolution is derived; the observed baryon-to-photon ratio η ≈ 6 × 10⁻¹⁰ is naturally reproduced for plausible ALP parameters; ALP–photon coupling generates a unique CMB spectral distortion that asymptotes to a constant at low frequencies, distinct from standard y- and μ-type distortions.
AI.conclusion: Axion-like particles provide a viable, testable pathway to baryogenesis through topological gauge dynamics, and their photon coupling yields a characteristic CMB distortion signature—offering joint cosmological and astrophysical probes of ALP physics.

title: Radiative Signatures from Warp Drives Traveling Through the Earth's Atmosphere
summary: We investigate the observable signatures of zero ADM mass warp drive spacetimes traversing Earth's atmosphere. Numerical simulations indicate that an aircraft-scale spacetime bubble moving at relativistic velocities would have a pronounced observational signature, where interaction with the atmosphere can produce luminosities exceeding one terawatt. The signature of a spacetime bubble at rest or moving at low velocity relative to the Earth would not generate such extreme luminosities. These results establish observational constraints on spacetime-based propulsion operating within the terrestrial environment and provide a framework for identifying potential high-velocity signatures. In particular, a warp drive traveling through the atmosphere at speeds exceeding approximately 10% of the speed of light would produce a unique brilliant glow.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically simulates atmospheric interactions of zero-ADM-mass warp drive spacetimes, finding that relativistic (≳0.1c) traversal produces >1 TW luminosity—distinct from sub-relativistic or static cases—yielding observational constraints and a detectable 'brilliant glow' signature for terrestrial warp propulsion.
AI.motivation: To establish observational constraints on spacetime-based propulsion (e.g., warp drives) operating within Earth's atmosphere, and to identify unique detectable signatures distinguishing relativistic warp bubbles from sub-relativistic or static configurations.
AI.method: Numerical simulations of zero ADM mass warp drive spacetimes interacting with Earth's atmosphere, analyzing energy deposition, radiation emission, and luminosity as a function of bubble velocity (including rest, low-velocity, and relativistic regimes up to ~0.1c and beyond).
AI.result: A warp bubble moving at ≥10% c through the atmosphere generates luminosities exceeding one terawatt due to atmospheric interaction; static or low-velocity bubbles do not produce such extreme emission. This yields a distinctive, observable 'brilliant glow' signature specific to high-speed warp traversal.
AI.conclusion: Relativistic zero-ADM-mass warp drives traversing Earth's atmosphere are observationally constrained by their intense luminous signatures; the predicted >1 TW glow at ≳0.1c provides a concrete, testable astrophysical/terrestrial signature for detecting or ruling out such propulsion in near-Earth environments.

title: Conductors and superconductors in stationary spacetimes: generalized Schiff-Barnhill and Meissner effects
summary: Previous studies on conductors and superconductors in curved spacetimes, and the gravitationally-induced electric and magnetic fields in them, are mostly restricted to the limit of weak fields and low velocities. Also the observer-dependence of these phenomena are not discussed in the literature. In this article, following London's phenomenological approach to superconductivity, we consider the electrodynamics of superconductors in stationary spacetimes without employing any weak field or low velocity limit. To this end, first we define the 3-force acting on charged particles in gravitational and electromagnetic fields, and derive its explicit form in a general spacetime decomposition formalism. Then, to highlight the role of observers, we apply the force equation to the free charges in superconductors in stationary spacetimes in the two well known threading and slicing decomposition formalisms. Applying the stationary condition in the superconducting state, we arrive at the generalized Schiff-Barnhill and Meissner effects, which compared to the low velocity and weak field limit include extra terms originating from the recently introduced gravitationally-induced constitutive equations. To show the consistency of our approach, we also derive the generalized Meissner effect from the second London equation in stationary spacetimes.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes the Schiff-Barnhill and Meissner effects for superconductors in stationary spacetimes—without weak-field or low-velocity approximations—by deriving observer-dependent 3-force expressions in threading and slicing decompositions, and incorporating gravitationally-induced constitutive relations.
AI.motivation: To extend prior work on electrodynamics of superconductors in curved spacetime beyond weak-field/low-velocity limits and to address the neglected observer-dependence of gravitationally-induced electromagnetic phenomena.
AI.method: Uses London's phenomenological superconductivity framework; defines and derives the relativistic 3-force on charged particles in general spacetime decomposition; applies it in threading and slicing formalisms for stationary spacetimes; imposes stationarity in the superconducting state; cross-verifies via the second London equation.
AI.result: Derives generalized Schiff-Barnhill and Meissner effects containing new terms from gravitationally-induced constitutive equations; confirms consistency by independently obtaining the generalized Meissner effect from the second London equation.
AI.conclusion: Observer-dependent electrodynamics in stationary spacetimes yields physically distinct, non-perturbative corrections to superconducting screening and flux expulsion effects, revealing deeper coupling between gravity and quantum condensates.

title: Constraining ModMax Black Holes with EHT and GRAVITY Observations: Optical Signatures and Accretion Disk Properties
summary: In this work, we study photon propagation and the radiative properties of a thin accretion disk around a ModMax black hole and examine the effects of the charge $Q$ (i.e. $Q^2 = Q^2_e +Q^2_m$ is the total dyonic charge, with $Q_e$ and $Q_m$ denoting the electric and magnetic charges, respectively) and the nonlinearity parameter $v$. We determine the event-horizon, photon-sphere, and shadow radii and find that increasing $Q$ decreases these radii, whereas increasing $v$ shifts them toward their Schwarzschild values. Using the EHT shadow measurements of M87$^\star$ and Sgr~A$^\star$, together with the available mass and distance measurements, we perform an MCMC analysis to constrain the ModMax parameters. The strongest upper limits are found to be $Q<0.391$ and $v<4.153$ at the 95\% credible level. We also investigate a Novikov-Thorne thin accretion disk and generate simulated disk images using backward ray tracing. The observed flux increases with $Q$, while increasing $v$ produces a slight decrease in the disk brightness. These results show how the ModMax parameters affect the black-hole shadow and thin-disk emission and provide observational constraints on $Q$ and $v$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates photon propagation and radiative properties of a thin accretion disk around a ModMax black hole, constraining its dyonic charge Q and nonlinearity parameter v using EHT shadow data of M87* and Sgr A*, yielding 95% upper limits Q < 0.391 and v < 4.153; it also finds Q increases shadow flux while v suppresses disk brightness.
AI.motivation: To probe nonlinear electrodynamics via black hole shadows and accretion disk emission in the ModMax theory, and to constrain its parameters (dyonic charge Q and nonlinearity parameter v) using observational data from EHT.
AI.method: Analytical determination of event-horizon, photon-sphere, and shadow radii; MCMC analysis constrained by EHT shadow measurements of M87* and Sgr A*, mass, and distance; backward ray tracing simulations of Novikov-Thorne thin accretion disk emission.
AI.result: Increasing Q shrinks horizon/photon-sphere/shadow radii; increasing v shifts them toward Schwarzschild values; MCMC yields 95% credible upper limits Q < 0.391 and v < 4.153; disk flux increases with Q but slightly decreases with v.
AI.conclusion: ModMax black hole parameters significantly influence shadow geometry and thin-disk radiative output; current EHT observations place tight constraints on Q and v, supporting feasibility of testing nonlinear electrodynamics with black hole imaging.

title: Monsters and neutron stars
summary: Using dimensional arguments and other simple estimates, it is pointed out that a branch of nuclei with mass number A>10^7 could be metastable if they have close to maximal isospin. This branch is continuous with neutron stars. The fastest decay mode of these hypothetical metastable nuclei (which we call monsters) is through neutron evaporation. We present an estimate of the lifetime and show it could be more than 100 ps for A>10^{39}. We speculate about their creation in binary neutron star mergers, where we argue that their lifetimes could be extended further, and their presence could be detectable in gravity wave experiments of the near future.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that extremely massive nuclei (A > 10^7), with near-maximal isospin, could form a metastable 'monster' branch continuously connected to neutron stars; their dominant decay is neutron evaporation, with lifetimes potentially exceeding 100 ps for A > 10^39, and they may be produced—and further stabilized—in binary neutron star mergers, possibly detectable via upcoming gravitational-wave observatories.
AI.motivation: To explore the existence and stability of ultra-heavy nuclear systems bridging atomic nuclei and neutron stars, motivated by dimensional analysis and continuity arguments in the nuclear chart.
AI.method: Dimensional analysis and semi-empirical nuclear estimates to assess metastability, neutron evaporation rates, and lifetime scaling; qualitative astrophysical reasoning regarding formation in binary neutron star mergers.
AI.result: Prediction of a metastable 'monster' nuclear branch for A > 10^7 at maximal isospin; estimated lifetimes > 100 ps for A > 10^39; plausible production and enhanced stability in neutron star merger environments.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-heavy, isospin-saturated nuclei—'monsters'—may represent a previously unrecognized metastable regime linking nuclei and neutron stars, with potentially observable signatures in next-generation gravitational-wave experiments.

title: Radiation-reaction driven dynamics at the third-and-a-half post-Newtonian order in different gauges
summary: We consider the coordinate-dependent definition of the radiation-reaction force at the third-and-a-half post-Newtonian order for general orbits. In order to (partially) determine its expression we refer to the balance method, involving the energy and angular momentum lost by the system, the Schott terms, and the energy and angular momentum fluxes at infinity. Only the latter are gauge-invariant quantities when passing from a coordinate system to another. The gauge dependence of both radiation-reaction force and Schott terms is encoded in a set of gauge parameters entering their definitions. We show how to relate the harmonic-coordinate losses of mechanical energy and angular momentum by the system with the radial and azimuthal components of the radiation-reaction force in a different coordinate system expressed in terms of phase-space variables in a Hamiltonian framework. The advantage of this approach is that only the coordinate transformation between harmonic coordinates and coordinates and momenta in the new coordinate system is needed, without solving again the balance equations. We derive such a transformation for both Arnowitt-Deser-Misner and Effective-One-Body coordinates. In the latter case we also discuss some simplifying choices of the gauge parameters adopted in current waveform models. Finally, we show how to obtain the solution for the radiation-reaction correction to the orbit in the new coordinate system simply by transforming the harmonic-coordinate solution known in the literature. This is a remarkable simplification, since one can avoid to solve again for the radiation-reacted dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a coordinate-transformation-based method to derive radiation-reaction forces at 3.5PN order for general orbits, avoiding re-solving balance equations by leveraging known harmonic-coordinate solutions and transforming them into ADM or EOB coordinates via phase-space mappings.
AI.motivation: To systematically handle the gauge dependence of the radiation-reaction force and Schott terms at 3.5PN order, and to enable efficient derivation of radiation-reaction dynamics in physically motivated coordinate systems (e.g., ADM, EOB) without re-solving the full balance equations.
AI.method: Uses the balance method (energy/angular momentum fluxes, Schott terms, mechanical losses), identifies gauge parameters encoding coordinate dependence, establishes Hamiltonian phase-space relations between harmonic-coordinate mechanical losses and radial/azimuthal radiation-reaction components, and constructs explicit coordinate-momentum transformations to ADM and Effective-One-Body (EOB) coordinates.
AI.result: Derives explicit transformations linking harmonic-coordinate radiation-reaction dynamics to ADM and EOB coordinates; provides radiation-reaction-corrected orbital solutions in those coordinates by direct transformation—bypassing new integration of equations of motion; identifies simplifying gauge-parameter choices used in current EOB waveform models.
AI.conclusion: Coordinate transformations in a Hamiltonian phase-space framework provide an efficient, consistent, and gauge-aware route to obtain radiation-reaction forces and orbital evolutions in non-harmonic coordinates—significantly streamlining the construction of high-accuracy gravitational waveform models.

title: Gluonic nucleon energy correlators and fracture functions for Color Glass Condensate
summary: Nucleon energy correlators (NECs) and fracture functions provide novel tools for probing nucleon and nuclear structure at small $x$ through measurements in the target fragmentation region (TFR) of deep inelastic scattering (DIS). We investigate gluonic NECs and fracture functions using the Color Glass Condensate effective theory at eikonal accuracy. We find that only the unpolarized and linearly polarized gluon components in an unpolarized target are nonvanishing at this order, and that both are determined by the adjoint dipole $S$-matrix. Furthermore, we show that the linearly polarized gluonic NEC $h_{1}^{t,g}$ generates a characteristic $\cos 2φ$ azimuthal asymmetry in the DIS energy pattern in the TFR. Unlike analogous observables in the current fragmentation region, this asymmetry is governed by the ratio of the linearly polarized gluon NEC $h_{1}^{t,g}$ to the unpolarized quark NEC $f_{1}^{q}$, making it particularly sensitive to the saturation scale. Our numerical analysis shows that this asymmetry exhibits substantial nuclear suppression, providing a novel window into the onset of gluon saturation at the future Electron-Ion Collider.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gluonic nucleon energy correlators (NECs) and fracture functions in the target fragmentation region of DIS using the Color Glass Condensate framework; it identifies nonvanishing unpolarized and linearly polarized gluon components governed by the adjoint dipole S-matrix, predicts a cos2φ azimuthal asymmetry sensitive to the saturation scale, and demonstrates nuclear suppression in numerical results—offering a new probe of gluon saturation at the Electron-Ion Collider.
AI.motivation: To develop novel probes of nucleon and nuclear structure at small x via gluonic NECs and fracture functions in the target fragmentation region of DIS, where conventional parton distribution functions are inaccessible and gluon saturation effects are expected to dominate.
AI.method: Applies the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory at eikonal accuracy to compute gluonic NECs and fracture functions; derives analytical expressions for unpolarized and linearly polarized gluon components in terms of the adjoint dipole S-matrix; analyzes azimuthal asymmetries and nuclear modifications using CGC-based kinematic and saturation-scale dependence.
AI.result: Only unpolarized (f1^g) and linearly polarized (h1^{t,g}) gluon NECs survive at eikonal order, both determined by the adjoint dipole S-matrix; h1^{t,g} generates a distinctive cos2φ asymmetry in the TFR energy pattern, with magnitude controlled by the ratio h1^{t,g}/f1^q — making it highly sensitive to the saturation scale Qs; numerical evaluation shows significant nuclear suppression of this asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: Gluonic NECs in the target fragmentation region provide a theoretically clean, saturation-sensitive observable for the Electron-Ion Collider; the predicted cos2φ asymmetry, suppressed in nuclei, serves as a direct signature of gluon saturation dynamics beyond standard collinear factorization.

title: Ultracompact Anisotropic Stars and Gravastars in General Relativity
summary: We study static, spherically symmetric ultracompact objects in General Relativity with anisotropic stress. Using the covariant anisotropic equation of state and assuming homogeneous density, we construct a mostly analytical model admitting configurations beyond the Buchdahl limit and with compactness arbitrarily close to the black hole value. The solutions exhibit two regimes separated by a critical curve in the parameter space of compactness and anisotropy, associated with the divergence of the central pressure: regular anisotropic configurations with positive central pressure, and singular configurations with negative central pressure for arbitrary anisotropy. In the latter case, we show that introducing a thick shell removes the pressure divergence, yielding regular ultracompact gravastar configurations. We further construct both anisotropic and isotropic gravastar models using this thick-shell construction.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs analytical models of static, spherically symmetric ultracompact objects in GR with anisotropic stress and homogeneous density, surpassing the Buchdahl limit; it identifies two solution regimes—regular (positive central pressure) and singular (negative central pressure)—and resolves the latter via a thick-shell gravastar construction, yielding both anisotropic and isotropic regular models.
AI.motivation: To explore ultracompact objects beyond the Buchdahl limit within GR, addressing stability and regularity issues arising from extreme compactness and anisotropic stress—particularly the divergence of central pressure in highly compact configurations.
AI.method: Uses the covariant anisotropic equation of state and assumes constant energy density; solves the TOV-like equations analytically for static, spherically symmetric spacetimes; analyzes parameter space to identify critical behavior; introduces a thick-shell transition layer to regularize singular solutions and construct gravastar models.
AI.result: Derives a family of exact, mostly analytical solutions exhibiting two distinct regimes separated by a critical curve: one with finite positive central pressure (regular), another with divergent/negative central pressure (singular); demonstrates that a thick-shell regularization eliminates pressure divergence and yields physically viable gravastar configurations, both anisotropic and isotropic.
AI.conclusion: Anisotropic stress enables ultracompact configurations arbitrarily close to black hole compactness while remaining regular—provided a suitable thick-shell structure is adopted; this provides a robust, analytically tractable framework for modeling horizonless alternatives to black holes.

title: Periodic orbits and gravitational wave signatures from magnetic dipoles around magnetized Kerr black holes
summary: We study periodic orbits and the associated gravitational radiation of a magnetized (uncharged) test particle carrying a magnetic dipole moment with coupling constant beta, moving in the equatorial plane of a rotating, magnetized Kerr black hole immersed in an external asymptotically uniform magnetic field, starting from the effective potential derived for such particles. We compute the marginally bound orbit (MBO) and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) as functions of the black hole spin a and the magnetic coupling beta, and map out the allowed region of the orbital energy-angular momentum (L, E) plane for bound motion. We then classify periodic orbits using the topological zoom-whirl scheme of Levin and Perez-Giz, characterized by three integers (z,w,v) through the rational rotation number q=w+v/z, and construct a family of closed rosette orbits at fixed angular momentum. Using the numerical-kludge, restricted-quadrupole approximation for an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral consisting of a stellar-mass magnetized secondary orbiting a supermassive magnetized Kerr black hole, we compute the time-domain gravitational waveforms h_+(t), h_\times(t) produced by these periodic orbits and their frequency-domain characteristic strain, and compare the latter with the anticipated instrumental sensitivity curves of LISA, Taiji and TianQin. We find that the magnetic coupling βsystematically shifts the MBO and ISCO outward and lowers their orbital energy and angular momentum, that the zoom-whirl structure of the periodic orbits is imprinted directly on the burst-like morphology of the emitted waveform, and that the resulting gravitational-wave signals fall within the sensitivity band of upcoming space-based detectors for suitably close and massive sources.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational wave emission from magnetized test particles orbiting rotating, magnetized Kerr black holes, analyzing how magnetic coupling affects orbital dynamics (MBO/ISCO), classifying periodic orbits via zoom-whirl topology, and computing detectable GW waveforms for space-based detectors (LISA/Taiji/TianQin).
AI.motivation: To understand how magnetic dipole coupling modifies orbital dynamics and gravitational radiation from test particles around magnetized Kerr black holes, especially for extreme-mass-ratio inspirals relevant to future space-based GW observatories.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of effective potential for magnetized test particles; numerical computation of MBO and ISCO; topological classification of periodic orbits using Levin–Perez-Giz (z,w,v) scheme; waveform generation via numerical-kludge, restricted-quadrupole approximation for EMRI systems.
AI.result: Magnetic coupling β shifts MBO and ISCO outward and reduces their energy and angular momentum; zoom-whirl structure directly imprints burst-like features in time-domain waveforms h₊(t), hₓ(t); characteristic strain falls within LISA/Taiji/TianQin sensitivity bands for astrophysically plausible sources.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic dipole interactions significantly alter orbital stability and GW morphology in magnetized Kerr spacetimes, producing observationally distinguishable signals for upcoming space-based interferometers.

title: Multi-Channel Di-Higgs Production in the scNMSSM: From Exotic 8b to Boosted 8tau Signatures at the HL-LHC
summary: We investigate multi-channel di-Higgs signal prospects in the semi-constrained Next-to-Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (scNMSSM) at large-lambda/low-tan(beta) at the HL-LHC with sqrt(s) = 13.6 TeV and L = 3000 fb^{-1}. Building on our previous work, four benchmark points are selected from 66 viable SM-like candidates, spanning three di-Higgs topologies: exotic multi-b (h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8b, BP1/BP3), boosted multi-tau (h1h1 -> 4a1 -> 8tau, BP2), and SM-like (BP4). A complete signal simulation chain (MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia 8.316 + Delphes 3) is employed for 10^5 signal events per benchmark point. Background yields are estimated from published LHC analyses and are used only for indicative sensitivity projections. For the 8b topology (BP1: m_{a1} = 47.4 GeV, BP3: m_{a1} = 51.9 GeV), b-jet efficiencies of epsilon(>=4b) ~ 14% yield S ~ 14,000-16,000 events, potentially compatible with 5-sigma sensitivity under the simplified background model adopted. For the boosted 8tau topology (BP2: m_{a1} = 8.2 GeV), 82.4% of same-a1 tau-pairs have Delta R(tau,tau) < 0.4, below the standard jet cone radius, due to the large Lorentz boost gamma ~ 7.5. This topology yields epsilon(>=2tau) = 38.4%, a factor of ~21 above the SM baseline, but requires dedicated boosted a1 taggers due to irreducible multi-tau backgrounds. BP4 serves as a SM-like reference, consistent with existing HL-LHC HH projections. The Higgs self-coupling modifier kappa_lambda in [0.884, 0.951] is universally suppressed below unity. title: Quasinormal modes in effective loop quantum gravity and consequences for isospectrality
summary: We investigate the quasinormal mode spectra of axial and polar perturbations about the effective Ashtekar, Olmedo, and Singh black hole geometry within the hybrid approach to loop quantum gravity. We also compare our results with those previously obtained by del-Corral and Olmedo for the dressed metric approach. Starting from mode equations that are straightforward effective counterparts of the classical equations, we compute these spectra by means of a high-order WKB method with Padé resummation. The violation of isospectrality between axial and polar perturbations that was claimed to exist in the dressed metric approach persists with the hybrid quantization, with deviations of the same order of magnitude as in the former effective case, although slightly larger for the hybrid prescription. In both situations, the isospectrality breaking decreases with the cubic root of the squared black hole mass in Planck units, consistently recovering the classical Schwarzschild limit. In addition, we perform a careful assessment of the applicability of the WKB approximation to the present effective analysis, confirming the parameter regions where the method remains reliable and highlighting specific mode cases for which the approximation breaks down.

AI.tldr: This paper computes quasinormal mode spectra for axial and polar perturbations of the Ashtekar–Olmedo–Singh black hole in loop quantum gravity's hybrid quantization, using high-order WKB with Padé resummation; it confirms isospectrality violation—similar to but slightly larger than in the dressed metric approach—and analyzes WKB validity limits.
AI.motivation: To test robustness of isospectrality breaking in black hole perturbations across different effective LQG frameworks (hybrid vs. dressed metric), and to assess reliability of WKB methods in quantum-gravity-corrected spacetimes.
AI.method: Derives axial and polar mode equations as effective counterparts of classical Regge–Wheeler and Zerilli equations; solves them numerically via high-order WKB approximation augmented with Padé resummation; compares results against del-Corral & Olmedo’s dressed metric analysis; performs convergence and domain-of-validity analysis for WKB.
AI.result: Isospectrality violation persists in hybrid quantization, with deviations ~same order as dressed metric but slightly larger; scaling of breaking ∝ M⁻²⁄³ (in Planck units); WKB remains reliable except for specific low-ℓ or highly damped modes where approximation fails.
AI.conclusion: The isospectrality breaking is a robust feature across LQG effective black hole models, not an artifact of a particular quantization scheme; WKB with Padé is generally reliable but requires careful domain validation for quantum-corrected potentials.

title: Tricritical dynamics in $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures and QCD
summary: In this paper we study the universal critical dynamics near the tricritical points in $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures and QCD with two massless quark flavors. In particular, we use the real-time formulation of the functional renormalization group to understand how the tricritical region connects the $O(4)$ Model G dynamics of the two-flavor chiral phase transition to that of Model H for the QCD critical point with explicitly broken chiral symmetry. We show that in presence of an additional subdiffusive energy-like density, the tricritical dynamics inherits the strong dynamic scaling of Model G, where the critical fluctuations of order parameter and conserved $O(N)$ charges relax at identical rates. The strong scaling in the planar $O(2)$ case relevant for the $λ$-line and the tricritical point in the liquid $\mathrm{^3He}$-$\mathrm{^4He}$ mixtures arises as an interesting limiting case. Including the explicit symmetry breaking by the finite light-quark masses in QCD, the energy-like density of the tricritical dynamics mixes linearly with the $Z_2$ order parameter to eventually produce the characteristic slow fluctuations of the entropy per baryon near the QCD critical point.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates universal critical dynamics near tricritical points in ³He–⁴He mixtures and two-flavor QCD using real-time functional renormalization group; it shows tricritical dynamics inherits strong dynamic scaling (Model G) when a subdiffusive energy-like density is present, and explains how explicit chiral symmetry breaking (e.g., finite quark masses) deforms this into Model H behavior near the QCD critical point.
AI.motivation: To unify understanding of dynamic universality classes across disparate physical systems—specifically, how tricritical dynamics bridges Model G (chiral O(4) transition) and Model H (QCD critical point)—and to resolve how explicit symmetry breaking modifies dynamic scaling.
AI.method: Real-time functional renormalization group (FRG) applied to tricritical field theories; analysis of dynamic scaling exponents and mode-coupling structure under inclusion of conserved densities (e.g., baryon number, energy-like density) and explicit Z₂ symmetry breaking.
AI.result: Tricritical dynamics exhibits strong dynamic scaling (z = 2, identical relaxation rates for order parameter and conserved O(N) charges) due to coupling with a subdiffusive energy-like density; the O(2) planar limit recovers λ-line/tricritical behavior in ³He–⁴He; finite quark masses induce linear mixing between energy-like density and Z₂ order parameter, yielding entropy-per-baryon slow modes characteristic of Model H at the QCD critical point.
AI.conclusion: Tricritical dynamics is not a standalone universality class but a symmetry- and coupling-controlled interpolation between Model G and Model H; its observable signatures depend crucially on the presence/absence of subdiffusive modes and explicit symmetry breaking, enabling cross-system predictions for critical dynamics in condensed matter and QCD.

title: All You Need is not $Ω_\mathrm{gw}$: Beyond the Mean of the Cross-Correlation Estimator when Searching for an Astrophysical Gravitational-Wave Background
summary: Searches for the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) using ground-based detectors rely heavily on the cross-correlation estimator $\bar C_f$, whose statistical properties determine the theoretical foundation for inference frameworks built on it. Past analyses usually assume Gaussianity of $\bar C_f$, but this assumption has not been systematically tested for a background of astrophysical origin like the one produced by compact binary coalescences. In this work, we decompose $\bar C_f$ into three physically motivated components: (1) the mean intensity, (2) the geometrical shot noise, and (3) the polarization leakage, and we compute 90\% credible intervals for its cumulants up to fourth order for the binary black hole, binary neutron star, and neutron star-black hole populations by propagating local merger rate uncertainties. We find that for the upcoming LIGO O5 sensitivity, $\bar C_f$ remains effectively Gaussian for all three populations, validating current Gaussian likelihood frameworks. For Cosmic Explorer (CE), however, the $\bar C_f$ produced by binary black holes becomes non-Gaussian, with skewness and excess kurtosis of $0.31^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$ and $1.3^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$, respectively, in the most sensitive band over a one-year observation period. For binary neutron star and neutron star - black hole mergers, $\bar C_f$ remains largely Gaussian even at CE. These results indicate that the Edgeworth expansion provides an adequate leading-order description of the non-Gaussianity expected in the next-generation era, while also motivating the development of more sophisticated statistical methods for a more accurate treatment.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the Gaussianity assumption of the cross-correlation estimator $\bar C_f$ used in stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) searches, decomposing it into physical components and quantifying cumulants; it finds $\bar C_f$ remains Gaussian for LIGO O5 but becomes non-Gaussian for binary black holes at Cosmic Explorer sensitivity, motivating use of Edgeworth expansion and advanced statistical methods.
AI.motivation: To systematically test the Gaussianity assumption of the cross-correlation estimator $\bar C_f$—commonly assumed in SGWB inference but unvalidated for astrophysical backgrounds like those from compact binary coalescences.
AI.method: Decomposes $\bar C_f$ into three physically motivated components—mean intensity, geometrical shot noise, and polarization leakage—and propagates local merger rate uncertainties to compute 90% credible intervals for cumulants up to fourth order for BBH, BNS, and NSBH populations.
AI.result: For LIGO O5, $\bar C_f$ is effectively Gaussian across all populations; for Cosmic Explorer, BBH-induced $\bar C_f$ exhibits significant non-Gaussianity (skewness $0.31^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$, excess kurtosis $1.3^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$), while BNS and NSBH remain largely Gaussian.
AI.conclusion: The Gaussian likelihood framework remains valid for current-generation detectors but requires extension—e.g., via Edgeworth expansion—for next-generation observatories like Cosmic Explorer, especially for BBH-dominated SGWBs.

title: $|ΔI|=3/2$ non-leptonic hyperon decays in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory
summary: Inspired by the recent BESIII measurements of non-leptonic hyperon decays, we reexamine their $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory with the extended-on-mass-shell renormalization scheme. Using the same restricted set of diagrammatic topologies as in the early analyses in heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory, we assess the effects of relativistic corrections, explicit decuplet baryons, different spin-$3/2$ coupling schemes, and pion-loop contributions. Our results show that relativistic effects alone lead to only mild changes, while decuplet contributions, especially in the consistent-coupling scheme, significantly improve the fit quality. Pion-loop contributions further reduce the $χ^2$ values. We highlight the importance of the consistent coupling scheme in the decuplet sector for describing the selected $|ΔI|=3/2$ amplitudes.

AI.method: Covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory with extended-on-mass-shell (EOMS) renormalization; inclusion of diagrammatic topologies from early heavy-baryon analyses; systematic variation of relativistic corrections, decuplet baryon contributions (under both inconsistent and consistent coupling schemes), and pion-loop diagrams.
